original_payload.original_title: Contribution des Ambassadrices Mata Massu Doubara (MMD-FSSP) en faveur du FSSP
original_payload.original_body:
Zinder, 20 Nov (ANP)- Les ambassadrices Mata Massu Doubara (MMD) ont organisé vendredi à la Maison de la culture Abdoussalam Adam, une  mobilisation des ressources des groupements féminins des réseaux et fédérations en faveur du Fonds de Solidarité pour la Sauvegarde de la Patrie ( FSSP).
La cérémonie de lancement s’est déroulée en présence des autorités régionales et coutumières des  représentants des leaders religieux,du noyau régional du FSSP et des représentants de nombreux groupements féminins .
Dans son intervention la représentante du Gouverneur de la région de Zinder et membre du noyau  régional  Mme Aissa Modiéli a exprimé  au nom du premier responsable de la région en transmettant ses  salutations et encouragements fraternels  pour cette mobilisation en faveur du FSSP en guise de reconnaissance à l’appel lancé à Tillabéry par son  Excellence,le Président de la République, Chef de l’État le Général d’Armée Abdourahamane Tiani pour la mobilisation de cent(100) francs par personne pour le Fonds de Solidarité pour la Sauvegarde de la Partie”.
Mme Aïssa Amadou Moudiéli  s’est réjouie de la campagne de sensibilisation entreprise au profit du fonds de solidarité pour la Sauvegarde de la Patrie( FSSP).
Pour sa part,la  Présidente des Ambassadrices Mata Massu Doubara (MMD) Hadjia Mariama Maman a félicité les différents groupements pour avoir  massivement à cet appel avant d’exprimer ses remerciements aux autorités administratives régionales et coutumières et aux représentants des partenaires techniques et financiers et des  ONG CARE et  AFB ainsi qu’aux représentantes de plusieurs  structures des femmes.
“La  procédure des  ambassadrices du MMD est une nouvelle réforme entreprise par les orgasations féminines au profit  du Fonds Solidarité pour la Sauvegarde de la Partie(FSSP)’’.
Elle a appelé les groupements  féminins à s’investir pour apporter leur contribution citoyenne pour la mobilization des  ressources en faveur du pays.
“Les  ambassadrices Mata Massu Doubara( MMD) sont animées de bonne volonté pour répondre  à l’appel lancé par le Président de la République, Chef de l’État  pour la contribution de  cent francs (100) CFA par personne,a-t-elle ajouté.
La ‘’ mobilisation sociale des citoyens peut nous permettre d’investir pour assurer la sécurité et la souveraineté alimentaire de notre pays’’.
Elle a ’’ exprimé sa gratitude à tout ceux qui ont fait le  déplacement   pour répondre massivement à cette campagne de sensibilisation des groupements féminins Mata Massu Doubara( MMD) pour  qu’Allah nous  protège et nous accompagne dans nos foyers respectifs’’.
Auparavant le représentant de l’Administrateur délégué de la la ville de Zinder M. Mai Boucar  Aboubacar a dans son mot de bienvenue  salué la  présence massive des femmes dans  cette mobilisation des sensibilisation autour des idéaux du fonds de Solidarité pour la Sauvegarde de la Patrie( FSSP).
“En vous mobilisant massivement  sous l’impulsion des ambassadrices Mata Masu Dubara (MMD), vous démontrez  que vous êtes le cœur battant, l’âme et la conscience de notre société”,a-t-il dit.
“Le Concept MMD a prouvé sa capacité à transformer la vie de nos ménages par la solidarité, où  l’ épargne et l’ entreprenariat féminin, trouvent sa plus belle illustration dans cette action citoyenne, a-t-il fait remarquer.”
Au cours de cette cérémonie de lancement de la campagne de sensibilisation de mobilisation des ressources plusieurs intervenants ont tour à tour pris la parole notamment,le Représentant du Sultan du Damagaram,le Conseiller Spécial du Chef de l’État Elhadji Mohamed Souley,le Rapporteur noyau régional ,le représentant des leaders religieux et celles des groupements  féminins ont tous salué cette initiative tout en  invitant ses braves femmes à  repondre a cet appel du  Président de la République Chef de l’État pour aller de l’avant.
Il faut noter que cette cérémonie de lancement de la campagne de sensibilisation des ambassadrices Mata Massu Doubara( MMD) à travers les différentes structures a permis de  mobiliser  la  somme de 218.700 FCFA au profit du Fonds de Solidarité pour la Sauvegarde de la Patrie FSSP.

items.title: 52ème Coupe Nationale de football au Niger : la FENIFOOT dévoile le tableau de confrontations entre les 36 clubs retenus

original_payload.original_title: 52ème Coupe Nationale de football au Niger : la FENIFOOT dévoile le tableau de confrontations entre les 36 clubs retenus
original_payload.original_body:
Niamey, 20 Novembre (ANP)- Au Niger, la fédération nigérienne de football (FENIFOOT) a effectué, le vendredi 20 novembre 2026, le tirage au sort des tours préliminaires de la 52ème  édition de la Coupe nationale du Niger.
36 équipes retenues vont se lancer à la course vers le trophée national.
20 de ces 36 clubs sont les mieux qualifiés de la Ligue nationale, tandis que les 16 autres sont les meilleurs des différentes Ligues régionales.
Lors d’une cérémonie introductive,  le secrétaire général adjoint de la FENIFOOT, M. Adamou Mounkaila, a souligné qu’il s’agissait du démarrage d’un long processus qui permettra de déterminer le successeur de l’ASN NIGELEC, dernier vainqueur de la Coupe nationale.
Il a, en outre, noté que ce tour préliminaire réunit des clubs de la Ligue nationale (1ère  division) et de la Ligue régionale (2ème division), avant d’indiquer ces prochaines confrontations pourraient réserver des surprises.
« Peut-être nous feront-ils revivre le sacre de la saison où l’AS SONIDEP, évoluant en deuxième division, a remporté la Coupe nationale. Nul doute que l’une de ces équipes qui seront opposées aujourd’hui pourra nous faire vivre de telles épopées. Bonne chance à toutes les équipes de la Ligue nationale et de la Ligue régionale. Que la meilleure gagne », a-t-il laissé entendre.
Pour sa part, le directeur des compétitions de la FENIFOOT, M. Alaeddine Adrika, a expliqué que l’objectif était de retenir 16 équipes qui rejoindront les 16 clubs de la Super Ligue pour procéder à un nouveau tirage au sort des seizièmes de finale.
Selon lui, le processus est simple et comprend deux tours préliminaires. Au premier tour, les 36 équipes s’affronteront dans 18 rencontres afin de dégager 18 qualifiées.
À l’issue de cette phase, 14 équipes se qualifieront directement pour les seizièmes de finale, tandis que les quatre autres disputeront le deuxième tour préliminaire, à l’issue duquel deux équipes obtiendront leur qualification.
Les 18 rencontres du premier tour préliminaire opposeront les équipes suivantes : ZR1 – ZR2, RLC – Zaroumey FC, Dankassaoua – AS Liboré, Akokana FC – Soniantcha FC, Boboye FC – N’Dendi, Olympic FC – Telwa FC, ZAC – Lada FC, Dilerame FC – Jangorzo FC, AS Bourja – RCB, Barka FC – JSD, JS Ader – Alkali FC, N Tessaoua – Entente FC, AS Madaroumafa – AS Toudou, Kourfey FC – AS Alheri, Inter FC – NY2, Kandadji SP – Dangourmou FC, Toubal FC – Aigle FC, Galabi FC – EFY Yantala.

items.title: Tunisie: la militante pour les droits humains Sihem Bensedrine condamnée à cinq ans de prison

original_payload.original_title: Tunisie: la militante pour les droits humains Sihem Bensedrine condamnée à cinq ans de prison
original_payload.original_body:
Tunisie: la militante pour les droits humains Sihem Bensedrine condamnée à cinq ans de prison
Figure de la défense des droits humains en Tunisie, Sihem Bensedrine a été condamnée ce vendredi 20 novembre 2026 à cinq ans de prison. Elle était poursuivie pour des faits de corruption présumés commis lorsqu'elle dirigeait une commission chargée de la justice transitionnelle. Cette avocate de 76 ans a présidé l'Instance vérité et dignité (IVD), créée après la révolte de 2011 pour enquêter sur les violations des droits humains et les faits de corruption sous l'ancien pouvoir de Zine el-Abidine Ben Ali.
Publié le :  20/11/2026 - 23:24
2 min     Temps de lecture
La journaliste tunisienne et militante des droits de l'homme Sihem Bensedrine, figure de l'opposition et ancienne présidente de la Commission « Vérité et Dignité », accorde une interview à son domicile à Tunis, le 26 juin 2026.        © Fethi Belaid / AFP
Par :
RFI
Publicité
La défenseure des droits humains Sihem Bensedrine a de nouveau été condamnée ce vendredi 20 novembre 2026 à cinq ans de prison. Une nouvelle condamnation qui vise, selon des ONG des droits humains, à la «  harceler et la punir pour son militantisme  ».
L'avocate de 76 ans, qui a passé sa vie à lutter contre l’oppression et à défendre les droits humains, dénonce une décision politique. «  Aujourd'hui, on est sans voix. On est vraiment sans voix pour commenter ce verdict qui n'a vraiment rien à voir avec les plaidoiries d'hier. Il a à voir avec une décision arbitraire prise au niveau des autorités politiques. C'est un verdict politique qui n'a rien à voir avec le dossier,  dénonce-t-elle auprès de RFI.  Donc, oui, nous sommes sans voix, il n’y a rien à dire, c'est l'arbitraire dans toute sa splendeur.  »
Déjà condamnée à 25 ans de prison au mois de juin
Sihem Bensedrine avait déjà été condamnée   à 25 ans de prison en juin dernier,   dans une autre affaire liée à la même commission. Elle avait déclaré qu'elle est visée par des «  responsables qui prennent l'État en otage  » dans le but de «  régler des comptes  » et de «  discréditer notre travail  ».
Arrêtée en 2024 dans le cadre de cette affaire, elle a passé six mois en prison avant d'être libérée dans l'attente des recours engagés contre les condamnations prononcées à son encontre. Elle risque désormais d'être incarcérée à tout moment.
Dans un communiqué publié ce vendredi,   Amnesty International affirme que Sihem Bensedrine est «  punie pour son travail historique à la tête de la commission de justice transitionnelle  ». Cette commission a permis de mettre au jour des décennies d'abus de l'État.
Les organisations de défense des droits humains n'ont de cesse de dénoncer un recul des libertés sous la présidence de Kaïs Saied.

items.title: Une jeune génération d'artistes renouvelle la musique zimbabwéenne

original_payload.original_title: Une jeune génération d'artistes renouvelle la musique zimbabwéenne
original_payload.original_body:
Reportage Afrique
Une jeune génération d'artistes renouvelle la musique zimbabwéenne
Publié le :  21/11/2026 - 00:00
Écouter - 02:55
Le Zimbabwe voit sa scène musicale se renouveler avec une jeune génération d’artistes qui n’hésite pas à expérimenter différents genres, tout en s’inspirant de sons traditionnels et avec des messages à faire passer. Une musique présente fin octobre lors du grand événement panafricain consacré à l'industrie musicale africaine, ACCES Africa, qui s’est tenu à Johannesburg, en Afrique du Sud voisine.
Mary Anibal lors de la conférence ACCES Africa à Johannesburg.        © Claire Bargelès / RFI
Publicité
De notre correspondante à Johannesburg,
La voix envoûtante de Brandon Aura a stupéfié   la salle  . À 25 ans, celui qui est surnommé  «  The Folk kid » impressionne avec ses compositions accompagnées par sa guitare et chantées en anglais, shona ou encore ndébélé : «  Je pense que si je me suis lancé à écrire ce genre de musique, c’est parce que j’ai toujours aimé raconter des histoires. Je dirais que mon univers est profondément influencé par Oliver Mtukudzi, j’ai grandi en écoutant sa musique,  confie le jeune chanteur.  Mais je suis aussi inspiré par des artistes sud-africains comme Zahara, et également des artistes européens tels qu’Ed Sheeran ou encore le groupe London Grammar.  »
Né de parents zimbabwéens, Brandon Aura a grandi en   Afrique du Sud  . Dans son titre «   Run Boy », sorti plus tôt dans l’année, il parle aussi d’exil et de recherche d’une vie meilleure, une chanson qui entre en écho avec l’actualité locale et les questions de migration : «  C’est un texte qui raconte l’histoire des étrangers, des immigrés, que ce soit en Afrique du Sud ou ailleurs sur le continent. Une chanson dans laquelle ils puissent se reconnaître, qui relate comment ils tentent de fuir quelque chose,  explique le chanteur.  Grâce à la musique, je peux transmettre de la bienveillance, sensibiliser à certaines réalités. Et puis je prends aussi tout simplement beaucoup de plaisir à juste créer ma musique   !  »
Pour afficher ce contenu , il est nécessaire d'autoriser les cookies de mesure d'audience et de publicité.
Accepter
Gérer mes choix
À lire aussi  «Roots Rocking Zimbabwe», la bande-son des années avant l’indépendance
«    Les gens expérimentent beaucoup, et j’adore voir ça ! »
Autre style mais même énergie,   Mary Anibal  , 26 ans, se définit comme une militante et parle à travers sa musique des violences faites aux femmes ou encore des mariages forcés d’enfants. Le tout porté par les notes de son  mbira , une sorte de petit piano à pouces traditionnel dans toute la région : «  Avant, c’était un instrument principalement joué par les hommes, on considérait à tort les femmes comme impures, à cause de leurs règles, or c’est un instrument sacré et spirituel  » ,  souligne-t-elle.
Basée à Harare, elle observe la scène musicale de son pays évoluer et explorer de nouvelles directions : «  Aujourd’hui, il y a un grand vide, parce que nos grandes légendes nous ont quittés. Mais il y a aussi une nouvelle génération qui doit prendre le relais et faire vivre cet héritage,  s'enthousiasme la chanteuse . Il y a vraiment quelque chose qui se passe en ce moment. On ne se cantonne plus juste à la soul ou au RnB. On se laisse simplement guider par son inspiration. Les gens expérimentent beaucoup, et j’adore voir ça !  »
Même si la région est plutôt connue pour ses sons  amapianos , ces deux jeunes artistes sont bien décidés à suivre leur propre chemin et à faire entendre d’autres sonorités venues du   Zimbabwe  .

items.title: I learnt so much from Buhari – Tinubu

original_payload.original_title: I learnt so much from Buhari – Tinubu
original_payload.original_body:
General News  I learnt so much from Buhari – Tinubu
By  Philip Daniel Yatai   ·   6 hours ago   ·  5 min read
0-4064x3074-0-0#
✓
✓
By Grace Abe / Edith Tsokar
President Bola Tinubu says he learnt valuable lessons from former President Muhammadu Buhari, describing him as a leader, patriot and man of exemplary character.
Tinubu stated this on Thursday in Abuja while inaugurating Buhari’s three-volume authorised biography at a public presentation organised by the planning committee alongside May Publishing Limited.
The President, represented by his Special Adviser on General Duties, Dr Moddibo Aliyu, said Buhari’s life exemplified service, character and patriotism.
He said public servants were remembered beyond their lifetimes through their records and contributions to society.
“Time and again, when we begin to live after we are gone, we will all be outlived by our memories.
“This is even more so when we have devoted our lives to serving the public.
“We leave behind a record of service and memories that may inspire those who come after us.
This is why we have the courage to tell our stories,” Tinubu said.
He said individuals who occupied positions of authority could not afford the luxury of silence.
“If you refuse to tell your story, others will tell it for you. You may scarcely recognise yourself in their account.
“Some will write to malign us, while others will write to advance an agenda,” he said.
Tinubu described Buhari as a phenomenon who defied the familiar conventions of Nigerian politics.
“The late President Muhammadu Buhari was a phenomenon that defied the familiar art of Nigerian politics.
“His life confounded those who claimed to predict it and offered instruction to successive generations of leaders.
“As a principled leader, a former military Head of State and a democratically elected president, his organic following expressed something that his critics often struggled to explain: the people’s recognition of a man who lived differently,” he said.
The President said he learnt valuable lessons from Buhari, particularly his simplicity, patriotism and commitment to Nigeria.
“I learned so much from President Muhammadu Buhari as a leader and human being who was not drawn to worldly possessions, and as a patriot whose devotion to Nigeria endured beyond the offices he held.
“He told me that the dignity of office depends upon the character of its occupant.
“He also told me that a leader’s example continues to speak long after he is out of service,” he said.
Earlier, Chairman of the Planning Committee, Mr Suleiman Adamu, said the biography was designed to preserve the historical record of Buhari’s life.
He said Buhari’s life spanned more than six decades of Nigeria’s political and military history.
Adamu said part of the proceeds from the presentation would support research, archival preservation and public education.
He added that the funds would also support efforts to establish a Muhammadu Buhari Centre to preserve his legacy for future generations.
The chairman urged individuals, corporate organisations and government institutions to purchase copies for educational institutions and public libraries nationwide.
He said Buhari participated in repeated interviews, including discussions on difficult and controversial episodes of his life.
Adamu added that the former president also assisted the author in identifying relevant individuals, events and documents.
Former President of Niger Republic, Mahamadou Issoufou, described Buhari as a major figure in Nigeria’s political history and one of Africa’s best-known leaders.
Issoufou said he regarded Buhari as a compatriot and, beyond that, a kinsman.
“Today, in presenting this volume, we move from mourning to historical reflection, which belongs to the family, friends and contemporaries.
“History belongs to everyone, including generations to come,” he said.
The author and chief biographer, Dr Udu Yakubu, said the project took more than two and a half years to complete.
He said the process involved extensive interviews, research, journeys, document reviews, revisions and consultations with people who had interacted with Buhari.
Yakubu said Buhari’s participation gave the work historical significance, particularly as his personal account was complemented by testimonies from associates, advisers and political opponents.
He added that the biography examined Buhari’s life across different political eras, from his childhood in Daura and military career to his emergence as Head of State.
The work also documented Buhari’s return to power through democratic elections in 2015 and his administration between 2015 and 2023.
According to Yakubu, the biography comprises three volumes titled The Phenomenon, The Presidency and The Reckoning.
He said the first volume traced Buhari’s early life, military formation, participation in the civil war, emergence as Head of State and subsequent overthrow.
It also examined his period as a political detainee and eventual return to democratic politics.
Yakubu said the second volume focused on Buhari’s administration between 2015 and 2023, examining its policies, decisions, achievements, challenges and controversies.
He said the third volume assessed Buhari’s legacy in security, the economy, infrastructure, anti-corruption, governance, foreign affairs and social policy.
Yakubu said the publication was not presented as the final word on Buhari but as a contribution to continuing debates about his place in Nigeria’s history. (NAN)
Edited by Rotimi Ijikanmi

items.title: NCF urges federations to deploy technology for grassroots development

original_payload.original_title: NCF urges federations to deploy technology for grassroots development
original_payload.original_body:
Sports  NCF urges federations to deploy technology for grassroots development
By  Philip Daniel Yatai   ·   6 hours ago   ·  2 min read
✓
✓
‌‌‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍⁠‌⁠‌‌By Ijeoma Okigbo
The Nigeria Cricket Federation (NCF) has urged other sports federations to embrace technology and effective monitoring systems to strengthen grassroots development and expand participation across the country.
Musa Ehizoje, NCF Business Development Manager, made the call on Friday at the Nigeria Sports Summit in Abuja, where he shared the federation’s grassroots development strategy.
Ehizoje, who represented NCF President, Uyi Akpata, said technology had helped the federation monitor grassroots activities, verify participation figures and ensure accountability in its nationwide development programme.
He explained that the federation deployed a Geographic Information System (GIS) to track coaches’ activities, identify schools and verify locations where cricket was being introduced across the country.
“If a coach says he is in Abakaliki or Kafanchan in a particular school, we have software that allows you to put the name of that school.
“It gives us the coordinates of where you are at that moment,” he said.
He added that the federation maintained a database containing the names, classes and ages of children introduced to cricket to ensure accurate records of grassroots participation.
According to him, the system supports the federation’s target of introducing cricket to 200,000 new participants annually, an increase from its initial target of 20,000.
Ehizoje said NCF had nearly 100 staff, with more than 75 per cent serving as grassroots coaches and technical personnel responsible for developing the sport nationwide.
He added that national and regional development officers supervised the coaches, while quarterly performance reviews assessed their performance and ensured they met their respective participation targets.
“What is available to cricket is available to all sports. What we need is a mentality shift on how we can achieve the numbers,” he said.
Ehizoje challenged other federations to move beyond recommendations by developing practical implementation strategies and setting realistic annual participation targets for their respective sports.
He also emphasised the importance of deploying personnel with good character to grassroots programmes, noting that their conduct could influence young athletes’ attitudes and development.
“When you go to the grassroots, you must teach before you coach. Teaching the ethics and etiquette of each sport allows that child to be properly formed,” he said.
He further highlighted cricket’s social impact initiatives, including talent identification programmes in Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) camps, which had produced players now representing Nigeria internationally. (NAN)

” The class spans 11 programmes in the four of  our 11 faculties whose pioneer students have matured to graduation this year,” she said.
The vice chancellor further described as historic the convocation of the university’s pioneer postgraduate class of 24 made up of 18 Master of Science graduates,  five Master of Business Administration students and one Postgraduate Diploma student.
Oladipo paid tributes to the female gender,  noting that 70 per cent of graduands in the undergraduate category were women while 12 of the 13 distinctions in health science programmes were earned by women.

Adedoyin,  an Executive Council member in the International Press Institute, representing Nigeria and Africa, also congratulated the management of the university for the significant achievements recorded so far.
The week-long convocation ceremonies will feature among others a  community outreach programme,  convocation lecture, medical laboratory science induction, Chancellor’s Night Dinner and conferment of degrees.

original_payload.original_body:
Health  Lagos governor’s wife seeks deployment of family physicians to 774 LGAs
By  Folasade Akpan   ·   7 hours ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Oluwafunke Ishola
The wife of Lagos State Governor, Dr Ibijoke Sanwo-Olu, has called for family physicians to be integrated into Nigeria’s primary healthcare system.
She said their deployment across the country’s 774 local government areas would improve access to quality healthcare and address service delivery gaps.
Sanwo-Olu made the call on Friday in Lagos at the 29th Annual General and Scientific Meeting of the Society of Family Physicians of Nigeria (SOFPON).
The conference had the theme: ‘Primary Healthcare Without Family Physicians: Can Nigeria Afford the Gap?’
She described family physicians as essential to delivering accessible, continuous and patient-centred healthcare at the community level.
She advocated a grassroots approach, with family physicians strategically deployed across Nigeria’s 774 local government areas.
According to her, this would enable doctors to understand community health needs, monitor disease patterns and provide preventive care.
She added that such deployment would facilitate early detection of illnesses and strengthen relationships between physicians and residents.
Sanwo-Olu proposed a coordinated healthcare structure involving ward, divisional, local government and senatorial levels.
She said this would strengthen healthcare coverage while complementing existing primary, secondary and tertiary healthcare facilities.
She urged family physicians to become ambassadors of improved healthcare delivery and develop solutions suited to Nigeria’s peculiar challenges.
Sanwo-Olu also acknowledged the impact of medical professionals’ migration, stressing the need to improve working conditions and retain doctors.
She said the Lagos State Government recognised the importance of healthcare infrastructure and public-private sector collaboration.
Also speaking, the Medical Director of St Nicholas Hospital, Lagos, Dr Dapo Majekodunmi, described family physicians as patients’ first point of contact.
He said they provided comprehensive and continuous healthcare for people of all ages, including appropriate referrals to specialists.
Majekodunmi expressed concern that some Nigerians increasingly relied on personal assumptions and artificial intelligence to determine which specialists to consult.
“I advise that patients should first consult family physicians, who can assess their conditions and refer them to specialists when necessary,” he said.
While acknowledging AI’s growing contribution to healthcare, he said technology could not replace human judgement, empathy and personal interaction.
He also warned against unsafe healthcare practices, particularly administering intravenous drips at home without appropriate medical assessment.
Majekodunmi said stronger family medicine practices could discourage such practices through proper patient evaluation and treatment.
Similarly, SOFPON President, Dr Blessing Chukwukelu, called on the Federal Government to invest in physician retention and comprehensive primary healthcare.
Chukwukelu, represented by the society’s Vice-President, Dr Ibrahim Yakubu, urged the government to address doctors’ burnout.
She advocated improved working conditions, competitive remuneration and adequate funding of healthcare facilities to curb medical migration.
“Universal health coverage (UHC) cannot be achieved by funding disease-specific programmes alone,” she said.
She stressed that investment should prioritise holistic primary healthcare addressing infectious and non-communicable diseases.
Earlier, Chairman of the Conference’s Local Organising Committee, Dr Sixtus Ozuomba, described family medicine as central to integrated healthcare delivery.
He said the specialty provided preventive, promotive, curative and rehabilitative services.
Ozuomba urged the government to establish a coordinated primary healthcare system that brings medical services closer to communities. ( NAN )

items.title: Antimicrobial resistance threat to families, healthcare system – Expert

original_payload.original_title: Antimicrobial resistance threat to families, healthcare system – Expert
original_payload.original_body:
Health  Antimicrobial resistance threat to families, healthcare system – Expert
By  Folasade Akpan   ·   7 hours ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Lilian U. Okoro
Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) poses serious health and economic challenges to families, particularly children, elderly people and those with limited resources, a Clinical Microbiologist, Dr Philip Oshun, has warned.
Oshun of the Lagos University Teaching Hospital (LUTH), gave the warning during a presentation at Microbe Madness 2.0, organised in commemoration of World Antibiotics Awareness Week, observed annually from Nov. 18 to 24 on Friday in Lagos.
The  News Agency of Nigeria (NAN)  reports that WHO says Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is one of the most urgent global health challenges of our time.
It occurs when bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites do not respond to antimicrobial medicines. As a result, infections become difficult or impossible to treat, increasing the risk of disease spread, severe illness, disability and death.
The misuse and overuse of antimicrobials, including antibiotics, antivirals, antifungals and antiparasitics, in people, animals and plants, are driving the development and spread of AMR.
Lack of adequate access to appropriate new and existing vaccines, diagnostics and medicines also contribute to the problem.
Oshun highlighted the consequences of infections that fail to respond to available medicines, noting that AMR could prolong illnesses, increase treatment costs, cause loss of productivity and place additional pressure on healthcare workers and families.
“When antimicrobial resistance occurs, there are very few antibiotics that will be available. Sometimes, those antibiotics fail, and it becomes very costly,” he said.
He explained that resistant infections could require prolonged hospitalisation, repeated surgeries and rehabilitation, leaving families struggling with financial and emotional burdens.
Oshun cited the case of a six-week-old baby who developed pneumonia that failed to respond to first-line treatment, causing the infection to spread into the bloodstream and joints.
According to him, the child underwent repeated surgeries and rehabilitation over three years, demonstrating the devastating consequences of antimicrobial resistance on families.
He said the experience underscored the need for increased public awareness and behavioural change to prevent infections and promote responsible use of antibiotics.
“Most common colds are caused by viruses. Taking antibiotics will not change the cause of those infections,” he said, warning against indiscriminate antibiotic use.
The microbiologist advised Nigerians against taking antibiotics prescribed for other people, buying them without prescriptions or changing their treatment without consulting qualified healthcare professionals.
He stressed that antibiotics should only be taken when prescribed by qualified medical professionals, with patients adhering strictly to the recommended dosage and duration.
Oshun also identified regular handwashing, vaccination, safe food and water practices, proper wound care and respiratory hygiene as important measures for preventing infections.
He explained that antimicrobial resistance occurred when microorganisms developed the ability to survive medicines designed to kill or inhibit them, stressing that it was the germs, not the human body, that became resistant.
He, therefore, urged individuals and communities to promote accurate information, advocate clean water and sanitation, prevent infections and use antimicrobial medicines responsibly to combat the growing public health threat.
Ms Chidera Aneke, the Organiser of AHi, stated that creative arts could be used to promote health awareness and educate people on the dangers of antimicrobial resistance (AMR).
Aneke said art provided an alternative platform for communicating health information, enabling people to understand and relate to important health issues through creative expression.
She urged Nigerians to avoid self-medication, practise regular handwashing with soap and running water, and keep up with vaccinations to prevent infections and reduce the spread of antimicrobial resistance.( NAN )www.nannews.ng

By  Folasade Akpan   ·   7 hours ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Chidinma Ewunonu-Aluko
Prof. Jesse Otegbayo, Chief Medical Director (CMD) of the University College Hospital (UCH), Ibadan, has listed the installation of a liquid oxygen tank as part of achievements in the facility, as the hospital celebrates its 69th anniversary.
Otegbayo said this on Friday during a news conference held at the institution in commemoration of its 69th anniversary.
The  News Agency of Nigeria (NAN)  recalls that the hospital was established on Nov. 20, 1957.
Otegbayo said the hospital, as the nation’s premier teaching one, had evolved into a foremost tertiary healthcare institution, providing specialised services to millions of Nigerians and patients from neighbouring countries.
He said the strength of UCH was anchored on three pillars: clinical services, research and training.
He added that the hospital had contributed immensely to the development of doctors, nurses, pharmacists, medical laboratory scientists and other healthcare professionals making meaningful contributions across the world.
Otegbayo said UCH won the SCIMAGO rating as Nigeria’s No.1 Health Institution and secured approval of laboratory services for National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA)-enrolled staff.
The CMD said that the School of Nursing received National Universities Commission approval on Nov. 6 to offer a full-time Bachelor of Nursing Science degree in affiliation with the University of Ibadan.
He listed other achievements to include the procurement of a 500 KVA generator, commissioning of a new patient lift, new and refurbished house officers’ residences, new vehicles, and renovation of the hospital guest house.
Others, he said, were the commissioning of a dry chemistry analyser and five KVA solar inverter at the Private Suites and Family Medicine Department.
“We have 36 KVA solar inverter at the Universal Laboratory, two ultrasound machines and 12 KVA solar inverter at the Radiology Department, among others,” he said.
On ongoing projects, he listed the construction of an ultra-modern fire service station, General Out -Patient Department (GOPD) extension, Emergency Department extension, Hospice and Palliative extension, Computer and Anatomy Studio for the School of Health Information Management, etc.
Otegbayo said management remained conscious of the importance of staff welfare, capacity development, a conducive working environment and professional growth.
“Our guiding philosophy must continue to reflect the importance of staff welfare and patient comfort.
“These are not merely expressions; they must remain practical priorities in our policies, decisions and daily operations,” he said.
Otegbayo listed challenges including increasing patient demand, rising operational costs, need for continuous infrastructure renewal, shortages and retention of specialised personnel, and growing expectations of patients and their families.
“We must confront these challenges with courage, creativity, collaboration and strategic planning,” he said.
He said as the hospital looked towards its 70th anniversary and beyond, it must become even more innovative, technologically advanced, financially sustainable and globally competitive.
He added that its mantra, “Shared Vision for Excellence,” should remain a guiding principle in its daily activities.
He thanked the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, the Board of Management of UCH, the University of Ibadan, development partners and other stakeholders, as well as patients, alumni and retired staff.
“Above all, let us remember that the ultimate measure of our success is not simply the number of years we have existed, the size of our infrastructure or the number of services we provide.
“It is the positive difference we make in the lives of the people we serve,” Otegbayo said. ( NAN )www.nannews.ng

original_payload.original_title: Experts urge men to speak up on erectile dysfunction
original_payload.original_body:
Health  Experts urge men to speak up on erectile dysfunction
By  Folasade Akpan   ·   7 hours ago   ·  2 min read
✓
✓
By Stephen Adeleye
Health experts have urged men to speak up about erectile dysfunction and mental health challenges instead of suffering in silence, emphasising the importance of early medical intervention.
They made the call on Friday at the Federal Teaching Hospital Lokoja (FTHL) Men’s Health Summit 2026, themed, “Getting Back in the Game: Finding Solutions to Erectile Dysfunction.”
The experts emphasised that erectile dysfunction and mental health conditions were prevalent, treatable and should be addressed early through professional medical care.
The Team Lead of the Men’s Health Summit Collaborators, Dr Ayodeji Ogunmola, said the group comprised more than 25 specialists within the hospital who managed men’s health conditions across different medical fields.
“They include urologists, psychiatrists, physicians, surgeons, radiologists and nephrologists, among others,” he said.
Ogunmola, a Consultant Urologist, said the summit was designed to encourage men to pay greater attention to their health and seek appropriate medical care.
He said that November was globally observed as Men’s Health Awareness Month, popularly known as “Movember”, a combination of moustache and movement for men’s health.
He said the month provided an opportunity for men to check their health indicators, including blood pressure, blood sugar and prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels.
Ogunmola thanked the Chief Medical Director and hospital management for providing the enabling environment and support for the programme, which he said was expected to become an annual event.
He recalled that the 2025 edition focused on prostate cancer, leading to the establishment of a support group earlier this year.
On erectile dysfunction, he said many men had been “benched” by various factors, including medications, hypertension, diabetes and psychological challenges.
He said that data indicated that as many as 70 per cent of men would experience some form of erectile dysfunction at different points in their lives.
He added that the condition was no longer limited to older men, as younger men were also affected.
According to him, men face various challenges that could cause worry, anxiety, low mood, reduced energy and depression, with some resorting to alcohol and other harmful coping mechanisms.
He emphasised that the summit aimed to prevent men from reaching the point of suicide or becoming unable to function effectively in society.( NAN )

original_payload.original_title: World Children’s Day: UNICEF urges leaders to prioritise children’s rights in budgets, policies
original_payload.original_body:
Health  World Children’s Day: UNICEF urges leaders to prioritise children’s rights in budgets, policies
By  Folasade Akpan   ·   7 hours ago   ·  4 min read
✓
✓
By Muhammad Nur Tijani
The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) has urged Kano, Jigawa and Katsina governments to prioritise children’s rights in their budgets, policies and programmes.
The Officer-in-Charge of Kano UNICEF Field Office, Dr Serekeberehan Deres, made the call at the Zonal Children’s Summit organised to mark the 2026 World Children’s Day in Kano on Friday.
The  News Agency of Nigeria (NAN)  reports that the UN Universal Children’s Day  , now known as   World Children’s Day  , is an international observance dedicated to   fraternity and understanding between children   and promoting the aims of the UN Charter through action for child welfare.
It draws meaning from its link to the  Declaration   and the   Convention on the Rights of the Child  , milestone agreements affirming various rights for children,   and having their voices heard.
Established by UN General Assembly resolution in 1954, it started as a call for global solidarity and a platform to advance the well-being and rights of children worldwide.
The Kano UNICEF field officer, therefore, said children’s recommendations should guide government decisions on education, health, nutrition, clean water, protection and environmental safety.
In a speech delivered by the Chief of UNICEF Field Office in Kano, Shafeeq Ur-Rehman, Deres said the summit provided an opportunity for children from the three states to express their views and share  expectations for the future through drawings, videos and other creative presentations.
He said children were not merely waiting for the future, as they were already contributing to shaping it.
He added that this year’s World Children’s Day theme “My Day. My Rights. My Future” — highlighted the importance of protecting children’s rights and ensuring their access to essential service.
“Every child has the right to survive and thrive, to learn, to be protected and to be heard, whatever their gender, ability or circumstance.
“Children’s rights are human rights, and they must be protected everyday, not only on Nov. 20,” he said.
Deres urged government officials, particularly commissioners and senior government functionaries, to take the children’s recommendations to their respective ministries and agencies for implementation.
He also called on partners, the media, communities, teachers and parents to support children’s voices and translate their demands into concrete actions.
The UNICEF official said the organisation would continue to work with governments, communities and young people to ensure that every child enjoyed their rights.
He identified girls, children with disabilities, out-of-school children and those living in hard-to-reach communities as groups requiring special attention.
He said UNICEF was marking 80 years of its work for children, adding that its commitment to improving the welfare of children in Kano, Jigawa and Katsina remained strong.
Earlier, representatives of Kano, Jigawa and Katsina states, Hajiya Umma Dalhatu, Dr Hauwa Babura and Babangida Abdullahi, respectively, reaffirmed their commitment to promoting and protecting children’s rights.
They also commended UNICEF for its continued efforts and support towards improving the welfare, development and protection of children across Nigeria.
Similarly, Hajiya Aisha Albasu, who represented the Chairman of the State Universal Basic Education Board (SUBEB), Alhaji Yusuf Kabir, reiterated the state government’s commitment to supporting and protecting children’s rights.
She said the government would continue to collaborate with relevant stakeholders and development partners to ensure that every child had access to quality education, healthcare, protection and other essential services.
Representatives of the Children’s Parliament, Alamin Umar and Asma’u Anka, called for greater protection of children’s rights and increased investment in their education, health and general welfare to enable them to achieve their full potential.
They stressed the need for government and other stakeholders to provide a safe and supportive environment for every child to thrive, irrespective of background.( NAN )

items.title: UNICEF seeks increased investment, stronger partnerships to secure children’s future

original_payload.original_title: UNICEF seeks increased investment, stronger partnerships to secure children’s future
original_payload.original_body:
Health  UNICEF seeks increased investment, stronger partnerships to secure children’s future
By  Folasade Akpan   ·   59 minutes ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Mercy Sawok
The  United   Nations   Children’s   Fund   (UNICEF)   has   called   for   increased   investment,   stronger   partnerships   and   innovative   solutions   to   guarantee   every   child’s   survival,   education,   protection   and   development.
Charles Lolika, Acting UNICEF Representative in Nigeria, made the call on Friday in Abuja at the 2026 World Children’s Day celebration, themed, “Every child alive, thriving and learning: A shared responsibility.”
The event also marked 80 years of UNICEF’s global commitment to children’s welfare.
Lolika said the next phase of UNICEF’s work, beginning in 2027, required renewed commitment from governments, development partners, communities and other stakeholders to place children at the centre of national development.
He said that UNICEF had worked alongside governments and communities globally for eight decades, adding that its operations in Nigeria began in 1952.
The acting representative emphasised the importance of listening to children, saying their voices, ideas, dreams and future mattered.
Lolika acknowledged progress in maternal and neonatal health, school enrolment and sanitation but noted that Nigeria continued to face significant challenges.
He identified the high number of out-of-school children, particularly in northern Nigeria, as a major concern.
According to him, UNICEF, the government and partners were exploring alternative learning and skills-development opportunities, including apprenticeships and entrepreneurship, to support children unable to return to formal education.
He, however, said the initiatives were operating on a small scale because of funding constraints, adding that additional resources would enable their expansion.
On child protection, Lolika said UNICEF was advocating for the safety and release of children held hostage to enable their reunion with their families.
Also speaking, Lona Hvass, UNICEF Nigeria’s Chief of Communication, said progress was being made in tackling child malnutrition, although at a slower pace than desired.
Hvass identified the first 1,000 days, from conception until a child reaches two years, as critical for brain development and overall growth.
She emphasised exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months, proper maternal nutrition, healthcare and micronutrient supplementation.
She also urged employers to create supportive conditions that would enable working mothers to breastfeed their babies.
On immunisation, Hvass said Nigeria still had one of the world’s largest populations of zero-dose children, describing vaccination as essential to protecting children against preventable diseases.
She said UNICEF was collaborating with the government and trusted community members to address vaccine hesitancy and encourage parents to complete their children’s vaccination schedules.
Meanwhile, children at the event highlighted challenges affecting their education and development.
Shedrack Great, a student of the FCT School for the Blind, Jabi, Abuja, appealed for braille machines to improve learning opportunities for visually impaired pupils.
Great, who expressed ambition to become a writer, also decried inadequate recognition and sponsorship for talented children with disabilities.
He urged out-of-school children with special needs to enrol in schools and pursue their education.
Similarly, Stephanie Aliu of Junior Secondary School, Kubwa, called for improved education and nutrition, urging the government to support vulnerable children with food assistance.
Fatima Abdullahi of Wingate International School said every child deserved education and should be encouraged to pursue their dreams.
Earlier, Cristian Munduate, UNICEF Chief of Field Office, welcomed participants, describing the celebration as an opportunity to recognise children’s rights and achievements.
The event also featured presentations and activities by children to promote awareness of their rights and encourage their participation in decisions affecting their lives.( NAN )

items.title: WaterAid urges sustained investment in handwashing to curb outbreaks

original_payload.original_title: WaterAid urges sustained investment in handwashing to curb outbreaks
original_payload.original_body:
Environment  WaterAid urges sustained investment in handwashing to curb outbreaks
By  Tosin Kolade   ·   1 hour ago   ·  4 min read
✓
✓
By Adesewa George/Grant Onyeke
WaterAid Nigeria has urged the Federal Government to sustain investment in water supply and handwashing facilities to strengthen preparedness against infectious disease outbreaks.
The Country Director of WaterAid Nigeria, Ms Evelyn Mere, made the call on Friday in Abuja at a roundtable on handwashing for effective infection prevention and control of Ebola, diphtheria and other communicable diseases.
Mere said handwashing with soap and running water remained a critical defence against infections, but awareness campaigns alone could not guarantee sustained hygiene practices.
Citing the 2019 WASH National Outcome Routine Mapping (WASHNORM), she said although 81 per cent of household heads knew at least two critical times for handwashing, only 10 per cent demonstrated proper handwashing with soap under running water.
She said only 16 per cent of households had access to basic hygiene services, while 14 per cent of schools had basic water and sanitation services.
According to her, only seven per cent of healthcare facilities and 14 per cent of markets and motor parks had access to basic water and sanitation services.
Mere said Nigeria’s experiences during the Ebola outbreak in 2014 and COVID-19 pandemic in 2020 exposed gaps in water and hygiene infrastructure, adding that handwashing facilities were often abandoned after outbreaks subsided.
She said Nigeria had recorded more than 10,000 confirmed diphtheria cases and over 65,000 suspected cholera cases across 35 states in 2026, while a confirmed Ebola case in Abuja in October had heightened public health concerns.
She regretted that the National Roadmap to Hand Hygiene for All (2021–2025), launched in 2022, was neither costed nor implemented before its target period elapsed.
Mere said the roundtable, organised in partnership with the World Health Organisation (WHO) and the Federal Ministry of Water Resources and Sanitation, aimed to mobilise stakeholders towards sustainable investment in hand hygiene.
Also speaking, Mr Habu Jamilu, Director, Water Quality Control and Sanitation, Federal Ministry of Water Resources and Sanitation, said sustained handwashing required reliable water supplies, functional facilities, adequate funding and regular maintenance.
He called for improved WASH infrastructure in schools, healthcare facilities, markets and motor parks, as well as stronger community participation and coordination among the three tiers of government.
Jamilu urged stakeholders to review the national hand hygiene roadmap and incorporate its priorities into the next planning cycle, stressing the need to consider women, girls, children and persons with disabilities in WASH interventions.
Similarly, Dr Muzzammil Gadanya, Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) Pillar Lead for Ebola Virus Disease at the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), said average hand hygiene compliance among healthcare workers stood at 26 per cent.
Gadanya attributed the low compliance largely to inadequate WASH infrastructure and shortages of essential supplies, rather than workers’ negligence alone.
He said 33 per cent of healthcare facilities lacked basic drinking water, while 54 per cent lacked basic sanitation.
He urged government and development partners to prioritise infrastructure improvements alongside behavioural change, adding that healthcare workers should observe the five critical moments for hand hygiene to prevent infections.
Also, Mrs Kogbara Ayaba, Chief Scientific Officer and Deputy Director, Hygiene Promotion, Federal Ministry of Water Resources and Sanitation, called for an end to Nigeria’s reactive approach to disease outbreaks.
Ayaba said only seven per cent of healthcare facilities had complete basic water and sanitation services, while 40 per cent of Nigerians still practised open defecation.
She regretted that handwashing facilities installed during the COVID-19 pandemic were neglected after the immediate threat subsided.
“Knowing is not doing,” she said, calling for predictable funding, better coordination among government agencies and adequate provisions for routine maintenance of WASH facilities.
Ayaba also advocated climate-resilient infrastructure and greater community participation to ensure sustainable access to water and sanitation services.
“Nigeria must move from counting facilities to guaranteeing reliable, inclusive, climate-resilient facilities,” she said.
The roundtable was organised to promote handwashing as an integral part of Nigeria’s pandemic preparedness and public health strategy. (  NAN  )

items.title: APC supporters share money, cause traffic congestion ahead of Tinubu’s Ibadan rally

original_payload.original_title: APC supporters share money, cause traffic congestion ahead of Tinubu’s Ibadan rally
original_payload.original_body:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate in Oyo State, Sharafadeen Abiodun Alli, distributed cash to supporters and traders in Ibadan on Friday, as traffic congestion and heavy security deployment disrupted movement in several parts of the city ahead of President Bola Tinubu’s presidential campaign rally.
The rally is scheduled to hold on Saturday, November 21, at Mapo Hall in Ibadan, Oyo State.
The APC governorship candidate was seen handing bundles of ₦1,000 notes to party loyalists and distributing stacks of ₦500 notes to traders, including male and female market vendors, around Orita Merin Mapo Market in Ibadan.
A group of political supporters and scruffily dressed individuals, believed to be thugs, followed the candidate throughout his visit, cheering and chanting his praises as he moved around the market.
Alli, who represents Oyo South Senatorial District, was also sighted at Mapo Hall inspecting the stage and monitoring workers preparing the venue for Saturday’s rally.

items.title: Can Mauricio Pochettino save Man United from Premier League relegation?

original_payload.original_title: Can Mauricio Pochettino save Man United from Premier League relegation?
original_payload.original_body:
Manchester United will be led by a third manager in three years when Mauricio Pochettino takes charge of his first match since replacing  Michael Carrick .
The fact that the Premier League clash is against their fierce rivals Liverpool – the team that, with United, are joint record English top-flight champions – is an added twist to a sordid recent tale for the Manchester club.
Recommended Stories
list of 4 items    list 1 of 4  Leaders Arsenal travel to beleaguered Newcastle as Premier League returns
list 2 of 4  ‘Total error of judgement’: Drone operator removes United training footage
list 3 of 4  In Qatar, Nepali fans hope to see their cricket team reach Everest heights
list 4 of 4  From Kansas to the Casbah: How the World Cup built an unexpected friendship
end of list
When Sir Alex Ferguson retired after lifting a then-record 20th league title in 2013, the Red Devils had climbed to the biggest and richest club in the world.
Now, apart from not being able to claim a Premier League crown since 2013, they are laden with debt – and worse still, they sit inside the relegation zone.
Can Pochettino save Man United from relegation?
The last time United were relegated from the top flight was in the 1973–1974 season. That came only six years after one of the club’s greatest nights – the lifting of the European Cup (now the Champions League), making them the first English club to do so.
Their fall this time around has not come quite as quickly, with their last crowning as European champions in 2008, and they have not been relegated – yet.
Few expect them to be. It would be unthinkable given the changed landscape of the entire footballing world, which has become awash with finances that clearly separate the elite and their resources from the rest.
When  Pochettino  was introduced to the media for the first time on Friday, the gathered press did not mention the word “relegation” even once.
So the simple answer is: yes, he can save the club from relegation. The longer equation is that the alternative would surely be the greatest shock in the history of a game famed for upsets and underdogs.

items.title: Overturned boat carrying mourners to funeral kills at least four in Nigeria

original_payload.original_title: Overturned boat carrying mourners to funeral kills at least four in Nigeria
original_payload.original_body:
A boat believed to be carrying hundreds of people to a funeral has overturned in southern Nigeria, killing at least four people, according to police.
The overcrowded vessel capsized on Friday in Bayelsa State after a mechanical failure while travelling from the communities of Ayama to Ukubie, police spokesperson Musa Mohammed told the Reuters news agency.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items    list 1 of 3  Nigeria launches hunt for hundreds of kidnapped mosque worshippers
list 2 of 3  Niger’s military-led government says it contained mutiny: What next?
list 3 of 3  More than 80 reported abducted in Nigeria as police find human remains
end of list
He said the dead were two adults and two children.
Police said 24 people were rescued, with 19 treated at a local clinic, and five taken to a hospital in the state capital.
Search teams were still looking for more victims, police said. Police did not say how many people were on board, but some residents told Reuters there were at least 300.
Police said the driver fled and the vessel’s manager was taken into custody.
According to a statement from the Bayelsa State Police Command, the accident occurred at the river junction between the Oweikorogha and Otuan communities, in the state’s Southern Ijaw district.
The boat that capsized was travelling “for a burial ceremony”, the statement also said, adding that police are “coordinating efforts with local divers and other responders”.
Such boat accidents are common on Nigeria’s busy rivers and waterways, often caused by overloaded vessels, poor maintenance or failure to comply with safety regulations.
A similar incident occurred in August, when at least 51 died after a boat  sank in northwest Nigeria’s Sokoto State , and another in January, when at least 26 people drowned after a boat ferrying people from Jigawa to Yobe State capsized.

items.title: Fossil fuel talks deadlock pushes COP31 climate summit into overtime

original_payload.original_title: Fossil fuel talks deadlock pushes COP31 climate summit into overtime
original_payload.original_body:
The COP31 climate summit has gone into overtime as nearly 200 countries remain deadlocked over a draft deal that no longer mentions fossil fuels.
The two-week talks in Antalya, Turkiye, were due to end on Friday, when a late closing session approved some technical matters, but not the wider political deal.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items    list 1 of 3  Restoring nature is key to a more resilient future
list 2 of 3  COP31 opens amid energy crisis as activists demand climate action
list 3 of 3  Tensions rise over draft climate deal at COP31
end of list
“We are close to the finish line, but we are not there yet,” COP31 President and Turkiye’s Environment Minister Murat Kurum told delegates.
Environmental groups tracking the two-week conference said the meeting lacked ambition to address the ‌worsening climate crisis and was on track to be the “worst COP ever”.
A third draft is expected on Saturday, the AFP news agency reported.
The fossil fuel fight
An  opening draft  from cohost and lead negotiator Australia on Monday called for a faster phase-out of fossil fuels. A slimmer version on Thursday removed every mention of them after Saudi Arabia and other major oil and gas producers objected.
Oil producers have also  resisted similar language  at past talks, including at COP28 in 2023. The revised text also dropped a $120bn target for money to help poorer countries adapt to climate change.
The European Union said the draft “risks turning this climate COP into a fossil summit”. Panama, which signed a letter with a dozen other countries demanding “a clear transition away from fossil fuels”, threatened to walk away from the talks.
“It is not acceptable to have a COP or a cover document that does not even mention fossil fuels, and we simply will not put up with it,” Panama’s environment minister, Juan Carlos Navarro, told a news conference.

items.title: US lawmakers push for tougher AI chip rules amid China export crackdown

original_payload.original_title: US lawmakers push for tougher AI chip rules amid China export crackdown
original_payload.original_body:
United States lawmakers say more regulations are needed to protect advanced AI chips once they leave the country, even as they support the recently imposed chip export controls.
This week, the US Department of Commerce announced a  new rule to restrict  how advanced US AI chips can be accessed remotely in the wake of the previous Nvidia CEO’s affair with a suspected spy for Beijing. The move would close what officials described as a loophole that allows Chinese companies to tap into computing power through data centres in third countries, bypassing US restrictions.
Recommended Stories
list of 4 items    list 1 of 4  Bessent vs Lutnick: Who is winning the China chip debate?
list 2 of 4  Nvidia dismisses calls to reinstate Jensen Huang amid blockbuster earnings
list 3 of 4  US lawmakers launch probe into Lutnick’s actions amid Nvidia scandal
list 4 of 4  US signed off on sales of nearly 900,000 AI chips to China in six months
end of list
The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS), which sits under the Commerce Department, said the rule would require data centre customers in Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore and Brazil to apply for a special licence to buy advanced chips from US companies, including Nvidia, because they “present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion”.
“The export controls should have been in place, certainly,” Democratic Representative Pramila Jayapal told Al Jazeera. “I also think it’s a bigger conversation about who dominates the AI market. We should not have this consolidation of all the AI knowledge in a couple of companies because that poses an enormous threat on multiple levels, including national security.”
In October, Jayapal introduced a policy framework that would require every AI company operating in the US to obtain a federal charter in an effort to protect the public interest.
The AI charter, the framework says, is modelled after existing regulatory frameworks, combining the round-the-clock federal oversight, strict safety mandates, and structural separation built into national bank charters with the rigorous pre-release federal testing required for nuclear materials and dangerous weapons.

original_payload.original_summary: Washington has new rules restricting remote access to advanced US AI chips, but lawmakers want more.

items.title: How Chinese Culture Sparks Global Innovation for the LEGO Group

original_payload.original_title: How Chinese Culture Sparks Global Innovation for the LEGO Group
original_payload.original_body:
English News
How Chinese Culture Sparks Global Innovation for the LEGO Group
Discover how the LEGO Group leverages the CIIE to turn traditional Chinese culture into global blockbusters, driving sustained investment and sustainable manufacturing.
Alwihda Info
20 nov. 2026
A LEGO installation recreating the scroll painting "Along the River During the Qingming Festival" draws crowds of local residents and tourists at Westlake 66 in Hangzhou, east China's Zhejiang province, Aug. 5, 2026. (Photo/Xu Hui)
Par Gao Shi, People's Daily
Stepping into the LEGO Group's booth at the 9th China International Import Expo (CIIE), designed under the theme "Joyful Community," visitors are greeted by a setting featuring a flower shop, a subway station, and cozy city corners woven seamlessly into everyday life.
The LEGO Group cleverly aligned its brand ethos of "Joy of Creation" with the "Joy Economy" theme championed by this year's CIIE.
"We are participating in the CIIE for the 9th consecutive year. It has provided us with a unique opportunity to engage deeply with consumers," said Niels B. Christiansen, CEO of the LEGO Group.
"We will continue to invest in areas such as brand building, retail footprint, business operations, and sustainable development to bring the joy of creation to even more Chinese consumers."
The LEGO brand first entered the Chinese market in 1983. The Danish toymaker's deeper bond with China was forged over a "festive reunion dinner" at the inaugural CIIE.
Built from 615 bricks, the set captured a cozy home centered around a dining table with six chairs. Grandparents, parents, and two children sat around a feast laden with fish, dumplings, chicken legs, and crabs. Indoors, vibrant red Spring Festival flowers were displayed, and Spring Festival couplets and the Chinese character "Fu," meaning good fortune, were pasted on both sides of the door.
The LEGO Group debuted this set depicting the Chinese New Year's Eve dinner, and another themed on the dragon dance, at the inaugural CIIE in November 2018.
"For anyone familiar with the Spring Festival, this scene evokes many cherished memories," said Wen Xiaodong, a senior concept designer at the LEGO Group.
To everyone's surprise, the set depicting the Chinese New Year's Eve dinner sparked great enthusiasm among overseas fans.
Maciek Selinski, head of LEGO China, said the limited-edition set was originally planned exclusively for China and the Asia-Pacific market. However, overseas builders left messages online urging the group to launch Chinese-themed sets globally.
"We were thrilled to see that these products captured the hearts of not only Chinese consumers, but also fans worldwide who appreciate traditional Chinese culture," Selinski said.
"The CIIE offers us an exceptional platform to showcase products spanning all age groups and diverse interests, bringing the LEGO play experience to more children and families."
Traditional Chinese culture continues to spark new creative ideas for LEGO designers. At the 3rd CIIE in November 2020, the company launched the LEGO Monkie Kid series inspired by the Chinese classic novel "Journey to the West."
Two months prior, an animated series based on the same IP premiered in the U.S., the UK, Canada, Germany, and Japan, winning over LEGO fans globally.
As of 2025, the LEGO Group had debuted 34 new products at the CIIE, about two-thirds of which drew inspiration from Chinese culture, history, and traditional festivals.
As cultural exchange sparks innovation, it has also spurred the group to steadily increase its investment in the market.
"A company's long-term investment relies on the protection of innovation," said Robin Smith, vice-president and general counsel for China and Asia Pacific at the LEGO Group.
"The proactive support from the Chinese government in protecting the LEGO Group's intellectual property has given us immense confidence," Smith said.
"Such support empowers us to keep innovating, deepen localization, and invest in China for the long haul. Together, we will continue to foster and safeguard a fair market," Smith added.
In 2013, pursuing a strategy to align production closer to its key markets, the LEGO Group announced the opening of a factory in Jiaxing, east China's Zhejiang province. This is its first manufacturing facility in Asia.
To support the long-term growth of its business across China and the broader Asian region, the company announced an expansion of the Jiaxing plant in 2022 to boost production capacity.
"As an important manufacturing hub for the LEGO Group in the Asia-Pacific, the Jiaxing factory actively puts our commitment to sustainable development into practice," Selinski said.
The group is increasingly using renewable and recycled materials to produce LEGO bricks. These include tire components made from discarded fishing nets and recycled engine oil, alongside e-methanol synthesized from renewable energy and biowaste-derived carbon dioxide, which powers the production of over 90 types of sturdy, rigid brick elements.
In 2023, the LEGO Group launched a global trial to transition toward more sustainable paper packaging. Today, the Jiaxing factory has achieved full conversion across its paper packaging production lines.
"By leveraging the ripple effect of the CIIE, we have built a mature and comprehensive LEGO play ecosystem in China encompassing retail networks, manufacturing, brand experience, and LEGOLAND resorts," Selinski noted. "This has laid a solid foundation for our sustained growth in China," he added.
original_payload.original_summary: Discover how the LEGO Group leverages the CIIE to turn traditional Chinese culture into global blockbusters, driving sustained investment and sustainable manufacturing.
