items.title: FG records over 7,000 entries for 2nd TETFund Research Fair – Echono

original_payload.original_title: FG records over 7,000 entries for 2nd TETFund Research Fair – Echono
original_payload.original_body:
Education  FG records over 7,000 entries for 2nd TETFund Research Fair – Echono
By  Funmilayo Adeyemi   ·   3 hours ago   ·  5 min read
✓
✓
By Funmilayo Adeyemi
The Federal Government says more than 7,000 research and innovation entries have been received for the second Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund) National Research Exhibition.
The Executive Secretary of TETFund, Sonny Echono, disclosed this on Monday in Abuja at a news conference ahead of the exhibition scheduled to hold from Nov. 24 to Nov. 27.
Echono said more than 1,200 entries had been selected after a transparent assessment process for participation in the exhibition.
He said the number represented a significant improvement over the entries recorded during the maiden edition in 2024.
Echono said the exhibition was designed to bridge the gap between research findings, innovation, production and market utilisation to stimulate economic growth.
He said TETFund, through its interventions, had continued to support public tertiary institutions such as universities, polytechnics and colleges of education, in research, infrastructure, academic development and innovation.
According to him, the interventions have contributed to improvements in research and development, with outputs from Nigerian institutions gaining increasing international recognition.
“TETFund has recognised the wide spectrum of outputs of the research and innovation ecosystem and its strategic need to enhance the linkages of impressive academic performances to industry.
“The view of the above are in line with the renewed hope and prosperity agenda of President Bola Tinubu, whose main aims are to reforming the economy through the massive generation of jobs, the creation of wealth, and the improvement of the general welfare of Nigerians,” he said.
He said the research outputs cut across natural and medical sciences, technology, innovation, social sciences and the arts, contributing to the growth in the number of professors and PhD graduates.
He said TETFund introduced the National Research Fair in 2024 to showcase completed research projects, practical innovations and technologies with potential for commercial production and expansion.
“The main aim of the fair is to catalyse the strategic linkage of research results to innovation, production and development in Nigeria,” he said.
He said the 2026 edition, with the theme, “Research to Markets: Driving Innovation, Enterprise and National Prosperity”, was being organised in collaboration with the organised private sector.
According to him, the involvement of private sector organisations is expected to strengthen collaboration between researchers, investors, manufacturers and other stakeholders.
He said the exhibition would provide opportunities for showcasing innovative products and services, networking and exploring partnerships among researchers, venture capitalists, financial institutions and regulatory agencies.
“The time is now ripe for Nigeria to take its rightful place to stimulate our economy by leveraging on the intellectual assets of our people.
“Nigerians are intelligent people, we are very hardworking, we are very creative, we are innovative.
“But we must harness it and deploy it to grow our economy so that Nigerians can benefit from all these investments that we’re bringing in our institutions and our establishments, and that is the primary driving purpose,” he said.
Echono said the exhibition would feature research outputs from TETFund beneficiary institutions and other agencies, including the Federal Institute of Industrial Research, Oshodi, and the Defence Industries Corporation of Nigeria.
He listed participating private sector organisations to include the Manufacturers Association of Nigeria (MAN), Nigerian Association of Small and Medium Enterprises, Nigerian Association of Small Scale Industrialists and Nigerian Economic Summit Group.
Others, he said, were the Nigerian Employers’ Consultative Association, Bank of Industry and Bank of Agriculture.
The executive secretary also announced that an International Research and Innovation Symposium would hold from Nov. 25 to Nov. 26 as part of the exhibition.
He said the symposium, with the theme, “Advancing Nigeria’s Innovation and Commercialisation for Global Competitiveness”, would bring together experts and institutions from within and outside the country.
He said participation in the exhibition was free, adding that members of the public, particularly prospective investors, were encouraged to attend.
Echono said Nigeria had abundant intellectual resources that could be harnessed to create jobs, generate wealth and address national challenges.
Speaking on efforts made to commercialise research findings, he said the Federal Government was creating platforms to connect innovators with investors and private sector organisations.
He said the involvement of financial institutions, manufacturers and venture capitalists would enable investors to identify viable innovations and support their transition from prototypes to market-ready products.
He added that TETFund was supporting innovators to secure patents and protect their intellectual property to prevent the theft or unauthorised exploitation of their inventions.
Also speaking, Mr Tamunoibuomi Okujagu, Acting Chairman, Research and Innovation Commercialisation Committee (RICC), said TETFund had developed a national portal to connect researchers, innovators, funders and private sector organisations.
Okujagu said the platform was designed to enable researchers to upload their inventions and innovations while prospective investors and funding institutions could identify opportunities for support.
He said the portal had so far recorded more than 14,000 entries, adding that 1,001 innovations claiming to be at the market-entry stage would undergo verification.
He said verified innovations would be matched with potential investors to facilitate the development of new products and services. (NAN) www.nannews.ng

original_payload.original_title: Nigeria records 94% HIV viral suppression – NACA
original_payload.original_body:
Health  Nigeria records 94% HIV viral suppression – NACA
By  Folasade Akpan   ·   4 hours ago   ·  4 min read
✓
✓
By Justina Auta
Nigeria has achieved 94 per cent viral suppression among people receiving HIV treatment, marking progress towards ending AIDS as a public health threat by 2030.
The Director-General of the National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA), Dr Temitope Ilori, disclosed this at a news conference ahead of the 2026 World AIDS Day commemoration in Abuja.
Ilori said Nigeria’s 2025 HIV treatment cascade showed that 80 per cent of people living with HIV knew their status, while 98 per cent of those diagnosed were receiving antiretroviral therapy.
She added that 94 per cent of those on treatment had achieved viral suppression, reducing HIV-related illnesses, deaths and the risk of transmitting the virus.
“These figures demonstrate progress in identifying people living with HIV, linking them to treatment and supporting them to achieve viral suppression,” she said.
The NACA director-general, however, identified gaps in HIV diagnosis, stressing the need to ensure more Nigerians know their status and access uninterrupted treatment.
She said Early Infant Diagnosis coverage among HIV-exposed infants increased from 15 per cent in 2022 to 66 per cent in 2025.
“While this is significant progress, we must do more to ensure that no child is left behind,” Ilori said.
She said the 2026 World AIDS Day theme, “Ending AIDS Starts with Access: Equity, Ownership and Sustainability,” highlighted the need for equitable access to HIV prevention, testing, treatment and care.
“Access must not depend on where you live, what you earn or who you are. It is a right, not a privilege,” she said.
Ilori announced that NACA would unveil the National HIV Domestic Resource Mobilisation and Sustainability Strategy 2026–2030 on Dec. 1, as part of the World AIDS Day commemoration.
According to her, the strategy will strengthen domestic financing, promote national ownership and sustain Nigeria’s HIV response amid declining global health funding.
She also announced plans for a National Prevention Conference to explore innovative HIV prevention approaches, including self-testing, pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) and emerging prevention technologies.
Dr Adebobola Bashorun, National Coordinator, National AIDS, Viral Hepatitis and STIs Control Programme (NASCP), said innovations would only save lives if they were accessible and affordable.
“We can have the best technology and products, but without access they are useless,” he said.
Bashorun said Nigeria was scaling up injectable HIV prevention medicines, oral PrEP and interventions to prevent mother-to-child transmission.
UNAIDS Country Director, Ms Tina Boonto, said more than 1.5 million Nigerians living with HIV were accessing antiretroviral treatment.
She, however, said Nigeria recorded about 64,000 new HIV infections annually, far above the fewer than 5,000 required to end AIDS as a public health threat.
“Ending AIDS starts with ensuring everyone can access the services, medicines, technologies and information they need,” she said.
Boonto called for increased HIV testing, expanded prevention services and stronger efforts to eliminate mother-to-child transmission.
Dr Patrick Dakum, Executive Officer, Institute for Human Virology (IHVN), represented by the Director of Prevention, Care and Treatment, Dr Helen Omuh, stressed the need for equitable access to HIV services, community ownership and sustained domestic commitment.
Dakum, speaking on behalf of implementing partners, reaffirmed their commitment to expanding effective interventions, strengthening domestic ownership and financing, and promoting sustainability.
“We want to affirm that ending AIDS requires more than service availability.
It requires equitable access, empowered communities, strong national ownership and sustainable investment.
“So together, we can build a resilient HIV response and accelerate Nigeria’s progress towards ending AIDS as a public health threat,” he said.
Mr Nicholas Ugbenyen, National Secretary, Network of People Living with HIV/AIDS in Nigeria (NEPWHAN), expressed confidence that access, equity, community ownership and sustainability would help Nigeria end AIDS.
Mrs Esther Hindi, National Coordinator, Association of Women Living with HIV/AIDS (ASHWAN), called for stronger efforts to prevent mother-to-child transmission.
“For us and for every pregnant woman out there carrying a baby, we say prevention is better than cure.
“We need to protect our unborn children from HIV so that they can have a strong future,” she said.
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the 2026 World AIDS Day will be commemorated on Dec. 1. (NAN)

items.title: FCT upgrades 20 PHCs under World Bank-supported IMPACT project – Official

original_payload.original_title: FCT upgrades 20 PHCs under World Bank-supported IMPACT project – Official
original_payload.original_body:
Health  FCT upgrades 20 PHCs under World Bank-supported IMPACT project – Official
By  Philip Daniel Yatai   ·   5 hours ago   ·  5 min read
0-0x0-0-0#
✓
✓
By Philip Yatai
The Federal Capital Territory Administration (FCTA) has upgraded 20 Primary Health Centres (PHCs) across the territory under the World Bank-supported IMPACT project to strengthen the delivery of quality and affordable healthcare.
Dr Adedolapo Fasawe, Mandate Secretary, FCT Health Services and Environment Secretariat, said this on Monday in Abuja, during the project’s community engagement and inauguration of the renovated and upgraded Owner-Occupier Model PHC, Kubwa, Abuja.
The  News Agency of Nigeria (NAN)  reports that IMPACT stands for Immunisation Plus and Malaria Progress by Accelerating Coverage and Transforming Services.
According to Fasawe, the move is to ensure residents, particularly women, children, the elderly and vulnerable populations, have access to quality and affordable healthcare.
According to her, the intervention goes beyond physical renovation, noting that the administration has also constructed staff accommodation, provided modern medical equipment, and installed solar-powered systems to guarantee 24-hour electricity and round-the-clock service delivery.
“The PHC is usually the first port of call for most residents. This is fundamental to improving health outcomes, reducing preventable deaths, and achieving universal health coverage.
“This is just one of 20 primary healthcare centres across different communities in the FCT that were upgraded under the IMPACT project,” Fasawe said.
She said that the FCTA’s healthcare intervention was anchored on three pillars—access, affordability and quality—in line with the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Bola Tinubu.
Fasawe commended the Minister of the FCT, Mr Nyesom Wike, for his massive road construction and rehabilitation projects across satellite towns, stating that the improved road network had drastically reduced travel time to health facilities.
She added that emergency response had been strengthened through the FCT Emergency Medical Services and Ambulance System (FEMSAS), which operates 24 hours free of charge and integrates local transport operators to convey pregnant women during emergencies.
To demonstrate the efficiency of the services, the mandate secretary asked a pregnant woman to call one of the emergency lines and the ambulance arrived at the scene in less than four minutes.
On affordability, the mandate secretary said that at least 1,000 vulnerable residents were being registered free of charge on the spot into the FCT Health Insurance Scheme under the Basic Health Care Provision Fund.
She explained that the initiative would grant them one-year free medical care in accredited public and private hospitals.
She urged traditional rulers and community leaders to take ownership of the upgraded facilities, monitor service delivery, and ensure that patients are not charged for free services.
“Healthcare should not be a luxury reserved for a few. Quality healthcare is your fundamental human right,” she added.
In his remarks, Dr Dan Gadzama, Executive Secretary, FCT Primary Health Care Board (FCT PHCB), said this on Monday in Abuja during a community engagement event organised under the project.
Gadzama explained that the Federal Government initiative commenced in 2021 with an initial completion date of December 2025, adding that while the project comprised both Immunisation and Malaria components, the FCT was initially excluded from the immunisation track.
“That trajectory shifted, however, due to Fasawe’s intervention, who pushed aggressively for the FCT’s inclusion in spite of initial scepticism that it was too late.
“She followed up and engaged with the World Bank, and in February 2025, the FCT signed its Subsidiary Loan Agreement (SLA) with the bank.
“Following subsequent disbursements in September and intense advocacy highlighting the capital’s unique status, the project timeline was extended by one year, setting the new closure date for December 2026,” he said.
According to him, the core objective of the IMPACT project is to drastically reduce maternal and under-five mortality by upgrading healthcare access points and removing financial barriers for vulnerable residents.
Gadzama listed key milestones achieved under the accelerated implementation to include the renovation and comprehensive equipping of 20 PHCs across the six area councils, selected through data-driven gap analysis.
He added that the board procured over 70 laptops and tablets to streamline data submission into the National Health Management Information System, and conducted specialised training for more than 250 healthcare workers across diverse intervention areas.
“We also procured and distributed ‘Mama Kits’—essential delivery commodities provided to eliminate financial barriers that typically deter pregnant women from visiting hospitals.
“In addition, we established active collaboration with community leaders, primary healthcare principals, and security agencies to ensure uninterrupted service delivery in security-challenged areas,” the executive secretary said.
Also speaking, Dr Onoriode Ezire, Task Team Leader for the World Bank IMPACT project, commended the FCT Administration for its execution speed and quality of work compared to states that joined the programme earlier.
“Some states that started this two years ago have not completed their PHCs, and they are not even up to your standard. It shows the type of leadership we have here, the commitment, and the work being done,” Ezire said.
Ezire, who recalled his role in establishing the legal backing for the FCT PHCB, urged residents to make optimal use of the upgraded facilities.
“The whole essence of this is not just for photographs, but for the health of our people. Please use these facilities scattered across the territory because your health matters to us,” he added.
Oner part, Senior Special Assistant to the President on Community Engagement (North-Central), Dr Abiodun Essiet, commended the FCTA for translating federal health policies into tangible benefits for residents.
Essiet noted that since 2023, the Federal Government had expanded health insurance coverage to over 16 million Nigerians and invested over N235 billion in upgrading primary healthcare centres nationwide, and providing free Caesarean sections and subsidised dialysis.
In his remarks, the Village Head of Usuma Ward, Kubwa, Chief Beje Tazodayi, lauded the FCTA for transforming the previously dilapidated clinic into a standard medical facility, and appealed for the absorption of volunteer health workers into the formal system. ( NAN )

items.title: CJID, partners, call for responsible AI use, protection of press freedom

original_payload.original_title: CJID, partners, call for responsible AI use, protection of press freedom
original_payload.original_body:
General News  CJID, partners, call for responsible AI use, protection of press freedom
By  Abdulrahman Kadiri   ·   3 hours ago   ·  4 min read
✓
✓
By Jessica Dogo
The Centre for Journalism Innovation and Development (CJID) and some other stakeholders have called for responsible use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and stronger media institutions.
They also called for sustainable journalism funding to protect democracy in Africa.
They made the call on Monday in Abuja, at the 2026 Media and Development Conference (MDC), where discussions focused on journalism, technology, democratic governance and the impact of AI on the media landscape.
The theme of the conference was, “Media, Technology and the Future of Democratic Societies”.
In his welcome address, the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of CJID, Dapo Olorunyomi, described journalism as an essential democratic infrastructure rather than merely a commercial enterprise.
Olorunyomi said independent journalism played a critical role in preserving national history, promoting accountability and providing citizens with credible information to participate in democratic processes.
He expressed concern over laws purportedly designed to combat misinformation in some West African countries, but increasingly used to suppress criticism and restrict freedom of expression.
He said that vaguely defined offences, disproportionate penalties and excessive executive powers to remove online content could create fear, encourage self-censorship and discourage investigative journalism.
Olorunyomi said that the regulations addressing digital harms must be necessary, proportionate, transparent and consistent with fundamental human rights, while enforcement should be subject to independent oversight and judicial review.
He called for stronger media institutions supported by credible internal policies, sustainable revenue models and professional development opportunities for young journalists.
He urged media organisations to move beyond dependence on short-term development projects and build lasting institutional capacity that would enable them to survive beyond external funding.
On AI, Olorunyomi said the technology offered opportunities for journalism through transcription, translation, data analysis and investigations into public expenditure.
He, however, warned against its potential to generate misinformation and reproduce existing inequalities.
He urged newsrooms to establish clear editorial policies on AI-generated content, ensure rigorous verification, protect confidential sources and uphold professional integrity.
In his remarks, Ronald Sonnemans, Deputy Ambassador of the Netherlands to Nigeria, said journalists globally faced increasing pressure, including harassment, threats, imprisonment and killings for performing their duties.
Sonnemans described journalism as the oxygen of democracy, adding that without free and credible information, democratic institutions gradually lost their ability to hold leaders accountable and sustain public trust.
He said that AI could help smaller newsrooms analyse large volumes of documents, support fact-checking and translate stories into local languages.
He warned against the misuse of AI to generate fake images, cloned voices and fabricated stories.
The envoy reaffirmed the Netherlands’ commitment to supporting press freedom through journalist training, dialogue platforms, innovative tools and research in partnership with organisations such as CJID.
Also speaking, Dr Kole Shettima, African Director of the MacArthur Foundation, described journalism as indispensable to functional democracy.
Shettima, who was represented by the Deputy Director MacArthur Foundation, Amina Salihu, said that citizens must not only receive credible information but also use it to engage government.
He urged development partners to support media organisations in ways that protected editorial independence while providing flexibility to respond to emerging challenges.
He expressed concern over limited awareness of Nigeria’s National AI strategy, urging journalists and media organisations to understand emerging policies and actively participate in technology and governance discussions.
According to him, the MacArthur Foundation’s priorities for the next five years includ young people, prosperity and ensuring that technology create opportunities accessible to all, while warning that unequal access could deepen existing social divisions.
He called for stronger collaboration among African journalists, researchers, policymakers and technology stakeholders.
He said that the continent must move beyond being merely a source of data to actively shaping and benefiting from the global digital economy.( NAN )
Edited by Kadiri Abdulrahman

items.title: Court grants INEC leave to amend defence in doctor’s suit

original_payload.original_title: Court grants INEC leave to amend defence in doctor’s suit
original_payload.original_body:
Judiciary  Court grants INEC leave to amend defence in doctor’s suit
By  Tosin Kolade   ·   3 hours ago   ·  4 min read
Court logo
✓
✓
By Edith Nwapi
An Abuja High Court on Monday granted the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) leave to amend its statement of defence in a suit filed by a medical doctor over the 2023 presidential election result uploaded by the electoral umpire on its IReV portal.
Dr Ephraim Okoye, approached the court in the case marked CV/2910/2023, claiming that INEC had a duty to conduct and transmit the result from his polling unit at Wuye, Abuja, in accordance with its due process and guidelines.
Presiding judge, Justice Peter Kekemeke, adjourned until Feb. 18, 2027 after the counsel to INEC, Mahmud Abubakar, was granted leave to amend his statement of defence.
Okoye claimed that prior to instituting the suit, he had written to the electoral umpire, requesting publication of the actual result and apology, but there was no response from the defendant.
His letter to INEC, written by his solicitor, according to the claimant, was dated March 8, 2023 and received by the defendant on the March 9, 2023.
He averred that in view of the defendant’s refusal to publish the actual result and apologise, he has suffered damage.
The claimant, therefore, sought “A declaration in the conduct and transmission of results from the polling units, the defendant owed the claimant a duty of care to ensure the results transmitted are the actual results from the polling unit.
“A declaration that the results for Finance Quarters 1, Wuye, eventually uploaded on INEC server by the defendant as the result of presidential election held on the 25/02/2023 are not the actual results from the said unit.”
He prayed for an order of the court directing the electoral commission to delete from the server the false results published for his polling unit .
He further sought an order of the court directing INEC to publish the correct Form EC8A for the unit signed by Nkwuda Precious Chizoba, dated February 25, 2023.
Also, he sought an order of the court directing the defendant to pay the sum of N50 million as damages for distress inflicted on him by reason of falsification of the results from his polling unit .
In addition, he sought N100 million in damages for the hours wasted by the defendant on Feb. 25, 2023.
Similarly, he sought an order of an apology published in two national dailies.
In its preliminary objection, INEC through its counsel, stated that election results and outcomes cannot be questioned in any manner other than by election petition before an election tribunal.”
The electoral body claimed that the claimant, was neither a political party nor a candidate in the election and has no locus standi to file the suit, it added that the court does not have jurisdiction to hear the matter.
Abubakar informed the court that the commission filed an application on notice, seeking to amend its statement of defence in the case.
With no objection to the application, Justice Kekemeke then granted INEC leave to amend its statement of defence and added that the claimant can respond if there is any need for such.
The claimant’s counsel, James Onyemaechi did not object to the application.
He then adjourned the case to February 18, 2027 for hearing.
The court had, on Monday, May 4, while ruling on INEC’s preliminary objection to the suit, held that the court has jurisdiction to hear the suit because the electoral body has a duty to ensure that election is free, fair and result reflects the outcome.
Justice Kekemeke held that the claimant’s allegation was that the electoral body breached its duty, adding that the claimant has a legal right to hold the defendant accountable by insisting his vote must count.
He further held that having actively participated in the election, the claimant has sufficient interest in the outcome of the election.
He held that, Okoye, like every other Nigerian voter, has locus standi to challenge and hold INEC accountable not only for the advancement of democracy but also the sanctity of the country’s electoral system
“Unlike other voters, he voted and waited for collation which was done. He snapped same, endured sun, rain and even rented a canopy to ensure accountability.
“It is imperative that the claimant has sufficient interest in the subject matter.
“Every Nigerian or voter has locus standi to challenge and hold the defendant accountable for the advancement of democracy and sanctity of our electoral system,” Justice Kekemeke ruled.
According to the judge, “The judiciary can no longer sit back and watch helplessly under the guise of not rocking the boat.
“Law is dynamic. Society must progress and accountability must be demanded of agencies of government.
“It is my view, and I so hold that the claimant has locus standi to bring this action.” (NAN)
Edited by Sadiya Hamza

items.title: Gouvernance financière de l’OMD-AOC : Les finances régionales passées au crible à Cotonou

original_payload.original_title: Gouvernance financière de l’OMD-AOC : Les finances régionales passées au crible à Cotonou
original_payload.original_body:
La neuvième réunion des comités financiers et d’audit de la région Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre de l’Organisation mondiale des douanes (OMD-AOC) s’est ouverte lundi 23 novembre à Cotonou. Accueillie à l’hôtel Les Orchidées de Cadjèhoun, cette rencontre de deux jours est consacrée à l’examen de la gestion financière régionale, avec en ligne de mire la transparence, la redevabilité et l’optimisation des ressources.
La gestion des ressources financières de la région Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre de l’Organisation mondiale des douanes est au cœur des travaux ouverts à Cotonou. Pendant deux jours, des experts régionaux et des membres des comités financiers et d’audit se penchent sur les mécanismes de gestion et de contrôle des ressources de l’institution. Placée sous le thème « Pour une douane innovante, intègre et performante au service du développement durable », cette réunion repose aussi sur l’intégrité, la transparence et la bonne gestion des ressources qui leur sont confiées.
La cérémonie de lancement a été marquée par le mot de bienvenue du directeur général des douanes du Bénin, le colonel Raouf Malèhossou Aboudou. Dans son intervention, il a souligné l’importance stratégique de cette rencontre dans un contexte où les administrations douanières sont confrontées aux exigences de mobiliser efficacement les recettes publiques nécessaires au financement du développement des États et garantir une gestion rigoureuse et transparente des ressources disponibles.
À ses yeux, les comités financiers et d’audit occupent une place essentielle dans cette dynamique. Leurs travaux contribuent, a-t-il expliqué, à préserver la pérennité des actions communes et à consolider la confiance des États membres ainsi que des partenaires techniques et financiers.
Les      points     inscrits à l’ordre
Au menu de cette session figurent notamment l’examen de l’exécution du budget régional 2026, la grille des contributions des États membres pour 2026-2027, les perspectives du budget pluriannuel 2027-2028 et le budget prévisionnel de l’exercice 2027. Autant de dossiers qui engagent la capacité de l’organisation à assurer une utilisation optimale des ressources mises à sa disposition.Les enjeux de cette rencontre ont été davantage explicités par Marcelin Laourou, inspecteur des douanes et coordonnateur du comité d’organisation, qui a rappelé que le fonctionnement de la région repose notamment sur les contributions financières des États membres.
Ces cotisations étant issues des ressources publiques, leur gestion, à l’en croire, appelle nécessairement des mécanismes de contrôle et de reddition de comptes. Il a ainsi précisé la complémentarité des deux instances.
Concernant chaque comité
D’après ses explications, le comité financier est chargé d’évaluer le niveau d’exécution du budget régional au titre de l’année 2026, d’identifier les difficultés éventuelles et de relever les insuffisances. Le comité d’audit, quant à lui, examine la gestion financière des différentes structures régionales, notamment la vice-présidence, les bureaux spécialisés et les centres régionaux de formation de l’OMD.
Au-delà du contrôle, l’audit doit également permettre de formuler des recommandations pour améliorer la gestion des fonds et renforcer la gouvernance des structures concernées. L’objectif est ainsi de promouvoir une gestion plus efficace et efficiente des ressources financières régionales. Les travaux mobilisent des experts issus de plusieurs pays, dont le Sénégal, le Gabon, le Togo, le Liberia, la Gambie et la République démocratique du Congo.
L’accueil de cette réunion constitue également une occasion pour le Bénin de renforcer sa visibilité sur la scène douanière internationale. Le directeur général des douanes a d’ailleurs mis en perspective cette rencontre avec plusieurs autres rendez-vous d’envergure prévus dans le pays. Cotonou doit notamment accueillir la 33è réunion du comité des experts, puis la 95è session de la Commission de politique générale de l’OMD, annoncée du 1er au 3 décembre 2026. Le 14è forum des fonctionnaires des douanes de l’UMOA est également programmé du 15 au 18 décembre 2026.

items.title: NPA marks 40 years in South Sudan, urges protection of civic space

original_payload.original_title: NPA marks 40 years in South Sudan, urges protection of civic space
original_payload.original_body:
Norwegian People’s Aid (NPA) has marked 40 years of humanitarian and development work in South Sudan, urging the government, donors and international partners to strengthen local civil society and ensure inclusive participation in the country’s upcoming general elections.
Speaking at the anniversary celebrations in Juba on Thursday, November 12, NPA Secretary-General Raymond Johansen said the organisation’s engagement in South Sudan began in 1986, when a convoy carrying food crossed from Kenya into Eastern Equatoria to assist communities affected by civil war.
Johansen said NPA had chosen to maintain its independence rather than participate in an operation in Sudan, insisting that its humanitarian work should not be dictated by those responsible for oppression.
The event brought together former Vice President Rebecca Nyandeng De Mabior, government officials, diplomats, development and humanitarian partners, civil society representatives, former NPA staff and a visiting delegation from Oslo.
Speakers recognised the organisation’s contribution to humanitarian assistance, peacebuilding, community resilience and development over four decades.
“Forty years later, we are still here. Still standing in solidarity with the people of South Sudan,” Johansen said.
NPA has supported healthcare, agricultural development, women’s empowerment, humanitarian assistance and efforts to strengthen democratic institutions.
Johansen said more than 800,000 patients had received treatment in hospitals supported by the organisation, including during periods of intense conflict and aerial bombardment. Nurses, midwives and other health workers trained through its programmes had helped deliver medical services to hundreds of thousands of people, he said.
In agriculture, NPA established a training centre in Yei, where farmers learned improved techniques that were later introduced in communities across the country.
The organisation also introduced ox-plough technology in the 1990s, helping farmers increase production while reducing the time and labour required for cultivation.
Johansen said NPA continued to promote improved farming methods to strengthen food security and reduce dependence on humanitarian assistance.
On women’s empowerment, he said an estimated 150,000 women had benefited from training programmes aimed at raising awareness of their rights and increasing their participation in public and political affairs.
“Women can do it,” he said, stressing the importance of women’s involvement in leadership and decision-making.
NPA has also worked in mine action, although insecurity previously forced it to suspend operations in the country. Johansen said the organisation had resumed activities through a small development project, with plans to expand its programme.
He warned that landmines and unexploded ordnance continued to threaten communities despite decades of efforts to address the legacy of conflict.
Civic space
Johansen said NPA currently supports more than 20 South Sudanese civil society organisations operating in different parts of the country.
The partnerships extend from Juba to Yambio, Bentiu and Kapoeta, supporting groups working on peacebuilding, women’s rights, media freedom, freedom of expression, civic participation and accountability in natural resource management.
He said civil society had grown significantly since the liberation struggle, when independent civic organisations were largely absent.
Johansen urged the government and international partners to continue investing in local organisations, describing them as essential to sustainable peace and democratic governance.
“To donors, partners and the government, keep supporting local civil society,” he said.
His remarks come amid concerns over restrictions on civic space, press freedom and the ability of civil society organisations to operate independently.
Aid concerns
Johansen warned that South Sudan faces serious humanitarian challenges driven by renewed conflict, declining international assistance and restrictions on humanitarian access.
He said the situation is being compounded by the war in neighbouring Sudan, which has placed additional pressure on communities and humanitarian operations.
He expressed concern about declining international assistance despite persistently high humanitarian needs, warning that conditions could deteriorate further without stronger intervention by the government and international partners.
With general elections approaching, Johansen called for meaningful engagement before, during and after the polls, saying civil society organisations, journalists and other stakeholders must be allowed to participate freely without intimidation or unnecessary restrictions.
He said an inclusive electoral process would be essential to building public confidence, strengthening democratic accountability and advancing the country’s political transition.
Food security
Johansen highlighted South Sudan’s agricultural potential, recalling that in December 2013 the World Food Programme declared an end to general food distribution following a strong harvest that year.
He attributed the achievement to investment in agriculture, saying it demonstrated what communities could accomplish with adequate support. However, renewed conflict broke out shortly afterwards.
He said the experience showed that investing in local communities, rather than relying solely on emergency assistance, could deliver lasting results.
“Investing in the people of South Sudan makes a difference,” Johansen said, pointing to the achievements of local organisations and communities despite difficult operating conditions.
Johansen reaffirmed NPA’s commitment to a peaceful, inclusive and democratic South Sudan, urging the government, donors and development partners to sustain humanitarian programmes, strengthen local institutions and protect the operating space for independent media and civil society.
He said the organisation’s 40-year presence demonstrates the importance of solidarity, investment in people and sustained partnerships in achieving lasting change.

original_payload.original_title: Ouadi-Rimé : L’ADIOR offre des fournitures scolaires et du matériel d’assainissement aux écoles de Djedaâ
original_payload.original_body:
Ouadi-Rimé : L’ADIOR offre des fournitures scolaires et du matériel d’assainissement aux écoles de Djedaâ
admin
novembre 23, 2026
2 minutes lues
109 vues
L’Association pour le développement intégré de Ouadi-Rimé (ADIOR) apporte son soutien aux établissements scolaires de Djedaâ. Ce lundi 23 novembre 2026, à l’École Centre de Djedaâ, elle a remis des fournitures scolaires et du matériel d’assainissement à l’administration éducative, en présence des autorités locales, des représentants des parents d’élèves et des enseignants.
Conduite par son président exécutif, Brahim Adjanta, la délégation de l’ADIOR a offert un lot composé de sacs scolaires, de cahiers, de stylos et de cartons de craies. Ces fournitures sont destinées à soutenir les élèves de la commune et à faciliter leurs conditions d’apprentissage. L’association a également remis du matériel d’assainissement pour contribuer à maintenir les établissements dans un environnement propre et sain.
Lors de la cérémonie, Brahim Adjanta a indiqué que cette initiative vise à accompagner les efforts de l’État dans le domaine de l’éducation et à contribuer à la mise en œuvre des politiques publiques en faveur de l’éducation pour tous.
À travers ce geste, l’ADIOR entend participer à l’amélioration des conditions d’apprentissage des élèves et à la promotion d’un cadre scolaire favorable dans le département de Ouadi-Rimé.

items.title: Tchad : la HAMA renforce les capacités de ses moniteurs en suivi et analyse des médias

original_payload.original_title: Tchad : la HAMA renforce les capacités de ses moniteurs en suivi et analyse des médias
original_payload.original_body:
La Haute Autorité des Médias et de l’Audiovisuel (HAMA) a lancé, ce lundi 23 novembre 2026 à N’Djaména, une session de formation de quatre jours destinés aux agents de son Unité de monitoring audiovisuel. L’initiative vise à renforcer les compétences des moniteurs en matière de suivi, d’analyse et d’évaluation des contenus diffusés par les médias.
Cette formation bénéficie de l’appui technique et financier du Projet d’Appui au Parlement et aux Processus Électoraux (PAPPE), financé par l’Union européenne et mis en œuvre par le Centre européen d’appui électoral (ECES).
La cérémonie d’ouverture a été présidée par le Secrétaire général de la HAMA,  Félicien Alladoum Radingaye , en présence du Coordonnateur adjoint du PAPPE,  Malam Jassy , des responsables de l’institution ainsi que des quinze agents bénéficiaires de cette session.
Cette initiative s’inscrit dans le prolongement de l’inauguration, le 24 septembre dernier, de la nouvelle Unité de monitoring audiovisuel de la HAMA. Celle-ci est dotée d’équipements permettant l’enregistrement continu des programmes de 22 stations de radio et de 8 chaînes de télévision, offrant ainsi à l’institution de meilleures capacités de surveillance du paysage audiovisuel tchadien.
Durant les quatre jours de formation, les quinze moniteurs seront outillés sur plusieurs aspects essentiels de leur mission. Les modules portent notamment sur la maîtrise des équipements techniques, les méthodes de suivi et d’analyse des contenus médiatiques, la connaissance du cadre juridique régissant les médias ainsi que les techniques de rédaction des rapports de monitoring.
Prenant la parole à l’ouverture des travaux, le Secrétaire général de la HAMA,  Félicien Alladoum Radingaye , a mis en exergue le rôle stratégique du monitoring dans le fonctionnement de l’institution. Il a rappelé que cet outil constitue un important instrument d’aide à la décision et de veille sur les pratiques des médias. Il a également plaidé pour un accompagnement renforcé en vue de développer les mécanismes de suivi de la presse en ligne et des plateformes numériques.
Pour sa part, le Coordonnateur adjoint du PAPPE,  Malam Jassy,  a réaffirmé la disponibilité de son projet à soutenir la HAMA dans le renforcement de ses capacités institutionnelles et opérationnelles.
À travers cette session de formation, la HAMA ambitionne d’améliorer les compétences techniques de ses agents, de garantir une meilleure qualité des observations, d’harmoniser les méthodes de travail et de consolider son dispositif de veille audiovisuelle.
Cette démarche traduit ainsi la volonté de l’institution de se doter de ressources humaines mieux qualifiées et d’outils performants pour assurer efficacement ses missions de régulation et de suivi du paysage médiatique tchadien, dans un contexte marqué par l’évolution rapide des technologies de l’information et de la communication.

items.title: CEN-SAD : Aboubakar Assidick Tchoroma officiellement installé au poste de Secrétaire exécutif par intérim à Tripoli

original_payload.original_title: CEN-SAD : Aboubakar Assidick Tchoroma officiellement installé au poste de Secrétaire exécutif par intérim à Tripoli
original_payload.original_body:
Le Ministre d’État, Ministre des Affaires étrangères, de l’Intégration africaine et des Tchadiens de l’étranger,  Ahmed Kougri , Président en exercice du Conseil exécutif de la Communauté des États sahélo-sahariens (CEN-SAD), a procédé, aux côtés de son homologue libyen,  Taher El Baour , à l’installation officielle de Aboubakar Assidick Tchoroma au poste de Secrétaire exécutif par intérim de l’organisation. La cérémonie s’est déroulée au siège de la CEN-SAD, à Tripoli.
Cette installation marque une nouvelle étape dans le processus de redynamisation de la CEN-SAD et son retour progressif à son siège statutaire en Libye, après plusieurs années de fonctionnement provisoire à N’Djamena, au Tchad. Elle intervient à la suite des décisions adoptées lors de la 22ᵉ session ordinaire du Conseil exécutif, tenue le 7 novembre 2026 à Tripoli.
Prenant la parole à cette occasion, le Ministre d’État,  Ahmed Kougri , a rendu un hommage appuyé au  Maréchal Mahamat Idriss Déby Itno , Président de la République du Tchad et Président en exercice de la Conférence des chefs d’État et de gouvernement de la CEN-SAD. Il a salué son engagement personnel et ses efforts en faveur de la préservation, de la continuité et de la relance de cette organisation régionale.
Évoquant les liens du Tchad avec la CEN-SAD, le chef de la diplomatie tchadienne a souligné qu’il ne revenait pas au sein de l’organisation en étranger, mais bien chez lui, mettant ainsi en avant l’attachement de son pays à cette institution. Il a, par ailleurs, insisté sur la nécessité de reconnaître les efforts et les sacrifices consentis par les personnels ayant assuré la continuité des activités de l’organisation durant son séjour provisoire à N’Djamena, tout en appelant au respect de leurs droits.
De son côté, le nouveau Secrétaire exécutif par intérim,  Aboubakar Assidick Tchoroma , a exprimé sa gratitude aux dirigeants tchadien et libyen pour la confiance placée en sa personne. Il a réaffirmé sa détermination à inscrire son mandat dans une dynamique de continuité institutionnelle, de rigueur administrative et de relance des activités de la CEN-SAD.
Parmi ses principales priorités figurent le rétablissement du fonctionnement effectif du Secrétariat exécutif, la clarification des situations administratives et financières, la préservation des acquis institutionnels ainsi que la préparation de la prochaine Conférence des chefs d’État et de gouvernement.
Il a également assuré que la mise en œuvre des conseils et orientations du Président en exercice de la CEN-SAD constituera un axe majeur de son action.
À travers cette installation, la CEN-SAD entend ainsi franchir une nouvelle étape dans son processus de redynamisation institutionnelle. Le retour progressif de son Secrétariat exécutif à Tripoli et la reprise effective de ses missions constituent des enjeux importants pour renforcer la coopération et l’intégration entre les États membres de l’espace sahélo-saharien.

items.title: Corridor Douala–N’Djamena : le ministre Amir Idriss Kourda évalue l’avancement des travaux d’extension de 20 km à l’entrée de la capitale

original_payload.original_title: Corridor Douala–N’Djamena : le ministre Amir Idriss Kourda évalue l’avancement des travaux d’extension de 20 km à l’entrée de la capitale
original_payload.original_body:
Dans le cadre du suivi régulier des grands projets d’infrastructures routières, le ministre des Infrastructures, du Désenclavement et de l’Entretien routier,  Amir Idriss Kourda , a effectué, ce lundi 23 novembre 2026, une visite de terrain sur le chantier du Projet d’amélioration de la performance du corridor Douala–N’Djamena (PCDN), Lot 1, reliant N’Djamena à Guélendeng et Bongor. Il était accompagné de ses proches collaborateurs.
Cette descente sur le terrain a principalement permis au membre du gouvernement de constater l’état d’avancement des travaux d’extension de 20 kilomètres à l’entrée de N’Djamena, sur le tronçon compris entre le rond-point de Walia-Barrière et Etena. Ce projet, considéré comme stratégique pour l’amélioration de la mobilité urbaine et le renforcement des échanges sur le corridor Douala–N’Djamena, fait l’objet d’une attention particulière des autorités.
Sur le chantier, plusieurs équipes de l’entreprise CGCOC sont mobilisées de jour comme de nuit afin d’accélérer l’exécution des travaux. Les interventions portent notamment sur les opérations de terrassement, la mise en œuvre de la monocouche ainsi que la pose de la grave-bitume, différentes étapes essentielles à la réalisation de cette infrastructure routière.
À l’issue de sa visite, le ministre a pu constater une évolution jugée satisfaisante des travaux, traduisant les efforts consentis par l’entreprise chargée de l’exécution. Toutefois, attaché au respect des délais contractuels et aux exigences de qualité,  Amir Idriss Kourda  a donné des instructions fermes à l’entreprise CGCOC, à la mission de contrôle et aux autorités municipales concernées.
Les orientations du ministre visent notamment à identifier et à lever, dans les meilleurs délais, les contraintes susceptibles de ralentir l’avancement du chantier. Une attention particulière a été accordée aux difficultés d’ordre technique ainsi qu’aux problèmes liés à l’occupation des emprises, qui nécessitent une coordination efficace entre les différents acteurs impliqués.
À travers cette visite de suivi, le ministre entend maintenir la pression sur les parties prenantes afin de garantir une exécution rapide et conforme aux normes de qualité requises. L’objectif est de permettre la livraison de cette infrastructure dans les délais impartis et d’améliorer durablement les conditions de circulation à l’entrée de la capitale.
La réalisation de ces 20 kilomètres supplémentaires constitue ainsi un enjeu majeur pour la fluidité du trafic, la sécurité des usagers et le développement des infrastructures de transport au Tchad.

items.title: India pledges $1.6bn in flood relief for Nepal as Balendra Shah visits Modi

original_payload.original_title: India pledges $1.6bn in flood relief for Nepal as Balendra Shah visits Modi
original_payload.original_body:
India will provide Nepal with a $1.62bn economic package in the wake of August’s  devastating floods  in the country, which led to the deaths and disappearances of thousands of people.
The sum announced on Monday is one of its largest-ever relief commitments, and comes as New Delhi boosts ties with its Himalayan neighbour, where it competes with China for influence.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items    list 1 of 3  More than 100 foreign trekkers stranded by floods in Nepal’s Gorkha region
list 2 of 3  Fire engulfs hotel in Nepal along Everest Base Camp route
list 3 of 3  One dead after two helicopters collide near Mount Everest in Nepal
end of list
The announcement followed talks between India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Nepali counterpart Balendra Shah, who is in New Delhi for a two-day visit – his first bilateral trip abroad since coming to power in March.
“We express our deep condolences for the loss of lives caused by the devastating floods in Nepal in August,” Modi said, standing alongside Shah in New Delhi. “To support Nepal’s reconstruction, and give fresh momentum to its long-term development, we announce a development cooperation package worth 240 billion Nepali rupees [$1.6bn].”
August’s floods, which scientists say were caused by the effects of climate change, were  triggered  when part of a mountain glacier collapsed and a torrent of water and mud flooded down into Nepal’s Rasuwa and Nuwakot regions, as well as into China’s Tibet region on August 26. More than 1,300 people have been confirmed dead, and more than 5,000 remain missing.
In October, the United Nations’ climate loss and damage fund set aside a sum of $20m for aid to Nepal.
India’s package will include a $377m grant for post-disaster reconstruction and new infrastructure projects, and a $1.24bn line of credit for energy projects, the countries said in a joint statement.

items.title: Danish top court’s ‘ghetto law’ ruling supports hardline immigration policy

original_payload.original_title: Danish top court’s ‘ghetto law’ ruling supports hardline immigration policy
original_payload.original_body:
Denmark’s top court has ruled that the eviction of “non-Western” tenants from a social housing estate under the country’s  “ghetto law”  was not discriminatory.
The Supreme Court on Monday rejected an appeal by seven families, after lower courts had dismissed their legal suits against the termination of their leases by landlord Boliggarden in 2022 on the basis that they had been discriminated against based on ethnic origin. The ruling backs Denmark’s tough stance on immigration.
Recommended Stories
list of 2 items    list 1 of 2  Why is Denmark separating ‘Western’ and ‘non-Western’ citizens?
list 2 of 2  Inside the fight against Denmark’s ‘straight up racist’ housing law
end of list
The country’s “ghetto law” housing legislation, adopted in 2018, allows for the ⁠relocation of residents from areas in which more than half of residents are “non-Western”.
It requires social housing estates to change the social mix by renting at least 60 percent of homes at market rates by 2030. The government has described the legislation as a bid to promote integration.
The seven families were among 91 that had their leases terminated in Helsingor, north of Copenhagen, most of them “non-Western”.
A lower court found in 2022 that the law’s criterion of “immigrants and descendants from non-Western countries” is neutral ⁠and not a measure of ethnic origin.
The Supreme Court on Monday upheld that, ruling “that applying the criterion of the law involves dividing people into two groups (people who are immigrants and descendants from non-Western countries, and all other persons)”.
original_payload.original_summary: The country's top court said eviction of 'non-Western' families did not constitute discrimination.

items.title: Tajikistan moves to leave ICC amid US push against court

original_payload.original_title: Tajikistan moves to leave ICC amid US push against court
original_payload.original_body:
The governing body of the International Criminal Court (ICC) has expressed concern after Tajikistan formally notified the United Nations of its decision to withdraw from the tribunal.
Tajikistan is the fourth country to begin the withdrawal process since the United States urged countries in July to leave the court. It follows Venezuela, Chad and Naoero, the Pacific island nation formerly known as Nauru.
Recommended Stories
list of 4 items    list 1 of 4  COP31 has failed. The climate system is working as designed
list 2 of 4  Anti-austerity strike spurs transport chaos across Belgium
list 3 of 4  Israeli restrictions cut off vital hearing aid supplies in Gaza
list 4 of 4  Nvidia board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
end of list
Tajikistan’s withdrawal from the Rome Statute, the treaty that established the court, is due to take effect on November 20, 2027.
The ICC prosecutes individuals for genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes and the crime of aggression when national courts are unwilling or unable to act. Its 2024  arrest warrants  for Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former Defence Minister Yoav Gallant over alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity in Gaza remain outstanding.
The administration of US President Donald Trump has  sanctioned  ICC judges and prosecutors as part of its pushback against the warrants for Israeli officials and an earlier investigation into the conduct of US forces in Afghanistan.
In July, the US State Department said it would seek to disable the court’s operations, portraying it as an enforcement arm of a “globalist bureaucracy” and accusing it of threatening US sovereignty.
In March, the ICC found that Tajikistan had failed to comply with its request to arrest Russian President Vladimir Putin during his visit in 2025. Putin is wanted by the court over alleged war crimes in Ukraine.

items.title: Israeli strikes kill at least three, including UNRWA worker, in Gaza

original_payload.original_title: Israeli strikes kill at least three, including UNRWA worker, in Gaza
original_payload.original_body:
Israeli air strikes have killed at least three people in Gaza, including a worker for the UN Palestinian refugee agency, according to the relief agency and local health officials.
The United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA) on Monday named the worker killed as Adel al-Helo.

He was working near a well in the Jabalia refugee camp in the enclave’s north when hit, the agency and medics said. Three others were wounded in the strike.
Later on Monday, another Israeli air strike ⁠targeted a vehicle in western Gaza City, killing two people and wounding others, medics said, according to the Reuters news agency. The Israeli military did not immediately comment.
Israel continues to launch attacks across the enclave, despite an October 2025 “ceasefire” deal with Hamas, which formally halted around two years of fighting but has failed to bring Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza to an end.
“The initial reports indicate that the strike hit a target on the street near the water well, which was manned by UNRWA staff and a guard. The staff were engaged in their regular duties associated with water well operations,” an UNRWA spokesperson told Reuters.
Israel has yet to respond to the incident. But since the October ceasefire, at least 1,679 Palestinian people and five Israeli soldiers have been killed.
Israeli forces have also continued to destroy residential buildings in Gaza, beyond the “Yellow Line”  to which they were required to withdraw under the ceasefire.

items.title: Russia warns Ukraine of ‘dangerous trend’ after Libya and Baltic attacks

original_payload.original_title: Russia warns Ukraine of ‘dangerous trend’ after Libya and Baltic attacks
original_payload.original_body:
Moscow has warned Ukraine that it will face “painful consequences” for its drone attacks on  Russian vessels  in Libya and the Baltic Sea.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters on Monday that Russia’s Ministry of Defence was handling the matter after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said his country’s forces had sunk two ships in the Libyan port of Benghazi.
Recommended Stories
list of 4 items    list 1 of 4  COP31 has failed. The climate system is working as designed
list 2 of 4  Anti-austerity strike spurs transport chaos across Belgium
list 3 of 4  Israeli restrictions cut off vital hearing aid supplies in Gaza
list 4 of 4  Nvidia board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
end of list
Peskov said the ministry would release details if it deemed it appropriate, adding that Russia will continue its attacks on Ukraine in response.
“Our military personnel continue to carry out large-scale, comprehensive strikes on military infrastructure in Ukraine on a daily basis. This practice has very painful consequences for the Kyiv regime,” he said.
Peskov added that the Baltic attack was “escalating tensions” in the region while he said Moscow hoped the Baltic states would use their influence to press Kyiv to stop what he described as “terrorist practices”.
Zelenskyy said on Monday that Ukrainian forces sank the Russian corvette Merkury at a naval base in Benghazi on Sunday and struck a cargo ship he said Russia used to carry weapons.
Libya’s eastern-based government, a rival to the country’s internationally recognised western government in Tripoli, has lodged a complaint with the United Nations, saying the attacks violated Libyan sovereignty. It called for an international investigation into reports that Ukrainian military personnel were allegedly present in western Libya.
original_payload.original_summary: Russia has reacted with fury to Ukraine's continued campaign targeting its naval and merchant shipping.

items.title: Police investigating bomb threats against schools in Germany and Denmark

original_payload.original_title: Police investigating bomb threats against schools in Germany and Denmark
original_payload.original_body:
Police are investigating bomb threats made against schools across Germany and Denmark.
Schools in the German capital, Berlin, and Danish capital, Copenhagen, were among those targeted, authorities said on Monday. The warnings, which were delivered via email, came after a wave of bomb threats across Europe earlier this month.
Recommended Stories
list of 4 items    list 1 of 4  Schools across Italy evacuated after receiving email bomb alerts
list 2 of 4  Bomb threats disrupt flights across Europe, no explosive devices found
list 3 of 4  Hoax or bomb threats? What we know about flight disruptions across Europe
list 4 of 4  Who is behind Europe’s suspected hybrid attacks?
end of list
As well as the capital, German police said schools in the states of Baden-Wurttemberg, Thuringia, Saxony-Anhalt and Rhineland-Palatinate were among the 450 schools affected across the country.
It was quickly concluded that the threats did not represent a “concrete danger” and were “not serious”, they added.
“At present, there is no evidence to suggest that the schools contacted so far are facing any specific threat,” police in the southwestern city of Freiburg in Baden-Wurttemberg said in a statement. Berlin police gave similar advice.
Authorities in the state of Thuringia said separately that they told schools to continue as normal because the perpetrators’ apparent intention was to scare people without taking action.
Police in the western state of Rhineland-Palatinate said in the “largely identical emails”, anonymous authors “claim to have placed explosive devices in school buildings and threatened to detonate them”.
The tabloid Bild reported that the subject of the emailed threat was: “Death awaits you.”
A Ministry of the Interior spokesman said schools were not being advised to evacuate because the incident fits into “the current overall threat picture”.
“I think both the schools and the security authorities of the federal states are prepared for such incidents and can then respond in a way that is appropriate to the situation,” he told reporters in Berlin, declining to comment on who might be behind the incident.
original_payload.original_summary: Bomb threats follow hoax emails sent to schools across Europe earlier in November.

items.title: Tchad : l’Assemblée nationale adopte le projet de loi de finance 2027

original_payload.original_title: Tchad : l’Assemblée nationale adopte le projet de loi de finance 2027
original_payload.original_body:
Les députés ont examiné et adopté ce lundi 23 novembre 2026 au palais de la Démocratie, le projet de loi de finance 2027. Adoptée en conseil de ministre le 5 novembre dernier, cette loi de finance, si elle est entérinée par le Sénat, franchit le seuil historique de 3000 milliards de Fcfa.
« La loi de finances est un acte majeur de prévision, de planification, de révision et d’autorisation budgétaire. Elle est également un recul des choix et d’options politiques », introduit le ministre d’Etat, Tahir Nguilin. Selon le ministre des finances, ce projet de loi de finances 2027 est « l’expression concrète de nos choix collectifs pour une vie meilleure, chaque jour, pour tous et partout au Tchad, dans la paix, la solidarité, la santé, l’espérance et l’équité ».
Selon le ministre Tahir Nguilin, le projet de loi de finance 2027 vise un double objectif : « accélérer la croissance économique et faire de cette croissance un congrès partagé avec nos territoires ». Ce projet de loi projette une croissance du PIB à 7,3% en 2027, contre 6% en 2026 et 5,9% en 2025. Selon le projet, les réserves hors pétrole augmentent de 20% comme toutes ces années grâce à la digitalisation progressive des principales régions. « La production pétrolière quant à elle est estimée à 148.556 barils par jour, contre 120.808 barils en 2026. Le PIB est retenu à 80$ le baril, contre 65$ le baril en 2026, avec une décote de 2% comme en 2026. Le taux d’échange régional du franc CFA par rapport au dollar est fixé à 600 francs CFA pour 1$, contre 550 francs CFA en 2026. Au demeurant, c’est pour la première fois que le budget de l’État, recettes et dons complets franchiraient le seuil symbolique de 3 000 milliards de francs CFA pour atteindre 3 070 milliards en 2027, contre 2 235 milliards en 2026, soit une progression globale de 25% », informe le ministre Tahir Nguilin.
D’après Tahir Nguilin, les recettes hors pétrole progresseraient à 1 313 milliards de francs CFA contre 1 094 milliards en 2026, soit une augmentation de 20%. « Les recettes pétrolières atteindraient 1 184 milliards en 2027, contre 780 milliards en 2026, soit une hausse de 52%, conséquence de l’augmentation combinée du coût du pétrole et du dollar, compensant largement la légère baisse de la production. Les dons, projets et les appuis budgétaires s’établiraient à 513 milliards, contre 401 milliards en 2026, soit une hausse de 43%, traduisant la vitalité de notre coopération économique.
Les dépenses prévues pour 2027 s’établiraient quant à elles à 3 007 milliards de francs CFA, contre 2 561 milliards en 2026, soit une progression de 19%. Les proclamations tiennent compte de l’évolution de la masse salariale et des régions de recrutement, des engagements contractuels de l’État, des charges de fonctionnement indispensables et de l’accélération des investissements prioritaires. Les dépenses personnelles représentent 796 milliards de francs CFA, contre 693 milliards en 2026.
Les biens et services de fonctionnement sont dotés de 213 milliards en 2027, contre 235 milliards en 2026. Les transferts et les subventions représentent 345 milliards en 2027, contre 305 milliards en 2026. Les investissements atteindront 1 458 milliards de francs CFA, dont 795 milliards financiers sur ressources intérieures et 673 milliards sur ressources extérieures, contre 1 512 milliards de francs CFA en 2026.
Les intérêts de la dette sont évalués à 134 milliards de francs CFA, dont 105 milliards au-dessus de la dette intérieure, comprenant notamment les intérêts sur les frais bancaires, les titres publics et les entrées obligatoires, contre 125 milliards de francs CFA en 2026.
« Le secteur de la santé bénéficiera d’un accroissement de plus de 70 milliards de francs CFA au titre de nos ressources propres ».
Selon le ministre d’Etat, Tahir Nguilin, cet effort vise à donner aux centres de santé et aux hôpitaux les moyens nécessaires pour remplir leurs missions où qu’ils se trouvent. « Une dotation supplémentaire hors de compte personnel de fonctionnement et d’investissement de plus de 14 milliards bénéficiera aux grands hôpitaux de N’Djamena, aux hôpitaux provinciaux et pour la première fois aux 15 hôpitaux confessionnels qui comptent le pays, aux 90 hôpitaux de district ainsi qu’aux 2 500 centres de santé qui comptent le pays. Cette dotation sera inscrite au titre des transferts. Les fonds destinés aux 2 500 centres de santé seront également inscrits au titre des transferts et non plus au titre des biens et services afin d’accélérer leur mise à disposition et de renforcer l’autonomie et la gestion des transformations sanitaires », explique le ministre. « Les transferts aux centres hospitaliers universitaires et aux grands hôpitaux bénéficieront d’une revalorisation de 20 à 25 % et des allocations additionnelles permettront à chaque hôpital provincial de disposer d’un minimum de 420 millions de francs CFA de budgets en plus de ces recettes propres. Certains hôpitaux provinciaux disposant déjà d’une dotation budgétaire largement superieur à ce minimum. Les investissements sur ressources intérieures progressent de 27 % pour financer la réhabilitation des infrastructures sanitaires et le renforcement des plateaux techniques », ajoute-t-il.
C’est par 177 voix pour, 0 contre et 4 abstentions que le projet de loi de finance 2027 est adopté par l’Assemblée nationale.

items.title: Festival N’DjamVi : une formation sur l’entrepreneuriat innovant en prélude à la 19ᵉédition

original_payload.original_title: Festival N’DjamVi : une formation sur l’entrepreneuriat innovant en prélude à la 19ᵉédition
original_payload.original_body:
En prélude à la 19ᵉ édition du Festival N’DjamVi, prévue du 25 au 28 novembre 2026, une formation sur l’entrepreneuriat innovant s’est tenue ce lundi 23 novembre 2026 à N’Djamena. Cette initiative vise à outiller les entrepreneurs, les porteurs de projets, les artistes ainsi que les acteurs des industries culturelles et créatives.
Organisée en partenariat avec l’Institut Kôrè des Arts et Métiers (IKAM) du Mali, cette formation s’inscrit dans le cadre des activités de la 19ᵉ édition du festival, placée sous le thème « Entrepreneuriat innovant et créatif ».
Lors de la cérémonie de lancement, le directeur artistique du Festival N’DjamVi, NGUINAMBAYE  Ndoua Manassé, a souligné l’importance de cette initiative : « Nous aurons en ligne les formateurs qui partageront avec nous leurs expériences, leurs connaissances, mais également nous donner les outils nécessaires pour ceux qui voudront bien entreprendre, pour ne pas trop tergiverser. Et je pense que ceux qui avaient commencé et qui ont été tergiversés pourront témoigner de pourquoi il faut avoir nécessairement les B.A.-BA pour continuer », a-t-il déclaré.
Il a également précisé les ambitions des organisateurs : « Notre ambition est très claire, c’est d’accompagner les talents, stimuler les idées dans la tête des entrepreneurs, mais aussi donner les outils afin que cela puisse aider véritablement. »
De son côté, le directeur général de l’IKAM, Keba Daffé, intervenant depuis le Mali, a réaffirmé son soutien et son engagement à accompagner les organisateurs du Festival N’DjamVi. Il a également insisté sur l’importance de placer les valeurs humaines au cœur de l’entrepreneuriat innovant : « Quand on parle d’entrepreneuriat innovant, souvent, les acteurs pensent surtout aux nouveaux outils et aux nouvelles technologies. Mais il est extrêmement important de garder également les valeurs, de fonder vos projets et vos entreprises sur ces valeurs, et de travailler avec les ressources humaines dans cet esprit. Je pense que si je devais dire quelque chose sur l’Institut, c’est véritablement cette particularité qui caractérise notre Institut », a-t-il souligné.
L’ouverture officielle de cette 19ᵉ édition est prévue le 25 novembre à partir de 16 h 30, au centre Olympe Africa, situé au stade d’Abena, également connu sous le nom de stade du 10-Octobre, à N’Djamena.
Au programme de cette édition figurent notamment des activités de sensibilisation, des prestations artistiques ainsi que des cérémonies de remise de prix et de récompenses. Le festival se poursuivra jusqu’au 28 novembre 2026.
Rahila BIASSOU TIL-NDECKA

items.title: Borkou : le PNT engage les communautés dans la lutte contre la stigmatisation des malades tuberculeux

original_payload.original_title: Borkou : le PNT engage les communautés dans la lutte contre la stigmatisation des malades tuberculeux
original_payload.original_body:
À Faya-Largeau, une séance de sensibilisation a réuni le samedi 21 novembre 2026, les autorités locales et les leaders communautaires autour de la lutte contre la stigmatisation et la discrimination des personnes atteintes de tuberculose. Cette activité a été organisée par le Programme national de lutte contre la tuberculose (PNT) qui renforce son action de sensibilisation dans la province du Borkou. C’est à travers une mission, conduite par son coordonnateur adjoint, Mahamat Saleh Idriss.
Prenant la parole, le chef de mission, Mahamat Saleh Idriss, a rappelé que la tuberculose constitue un véritable problème de santé publique et que sa lutte nécessite l’engagement de tous. Il a ainsi insisté sur l’importance de briser les préjugés qui entourent cette maladie et de favoriser un accompagnement digne des personnes atteintes.
Ouvrant officiellement la rencontre, le préfet du département du Borkou, Ouangrébélé Taokamla, a salué cette initiative qu’il a qualifiée d’importante. Il a souligné que la lutte contre la tuberculose figure parmi les préoccupations majeures des plus hautes autorités du pays. Le préfet a également invité les participants à transmettre les messages reçus à leurs familles et dans leurs communautés respectives.
Lire aussi :  Tuberculose : plus d’un million de décès en 2025, des progrès trop lents face au recul des financements
Animée par l’expert national en communication du PNT, Djimsangar Grégoire, cette séance a permis d’aborder plusieurs thématiques, notamment la tuberculose et ses facteurs de risque, les obstacles socioculturels ainsi que les messages clés pour prévenir la stigmatisation et la discrimination des patients tuberculeux.
À travers cette activité, le PNT entend renforcer la mobilisation communautaire et encourager des comportements favorables à la prévention, au dépistage et à la prise en charge de la tuberculose, dans un environnement exempt de préjugés et de discrimination.
Lire aussi :  Lutte contre le VIH, la tuberculose et le paludisme : les acteurs appelés à rationaliser les ressources

items.title: Borkou : deux présumés braqueurs arrêtés après la mort de deux commerçants

original_payload.original_title: Borkou : deux présumés braqueurs arrêtés après la mort de deux commerçants
original_payload.original_body:
Le délégué général du gouvernement auprès de la province du Borkou, le général Ibrahim Akhachane, a présidé, ce lundi 23 novembre 2026 à Faya-Largeau, une cérémonie de présentation de deux présumés braqueurs interpellés par les forces de défense et de sécurité. Ils sont soupçonnés d’être impliqués dans une attaque à main armée qui a coûté la vie à deux commerçants à Olboye, une localité située à une quarantaine de kilomètres de Faya-Largeau.
Selon les informations communiquées lors de la cérémonie, les deux individus auraient attaqué un véhicule transportant des commerçants avant de prendre la fuite après avoir tué deux personnes.
Alertées, les forces de défense et de sécurité ont immédiatement lancé des recherches, qui ont permis de les interpeller quelques heures après les faits.
Présent à la cérémonie, le chef de la division des renseignements, Idriss Togoye, a apporté des précisions sur les stratégies ayant conduit à l’interpellation des deux suspects.
Lire aussi :  Importante saisie d’armes et de munitions dans le Borkou
De son côté, le commandant de la zone de défense et de sécurité n° 7 du Borkou, le général Khalil Tahir Abdallah, a salué le courage, la détermination et la promptitude des forces engagées dans cette opération.
Le délégué général du gouvernement, le général Ibrahim Akhachane, a également félicité les services de sécurité pour leur intervention. Il a par ailleurs déploré la mort des deux commerçants et ordonné que les présumés auteurs soient remis à la justice.
Lire aussi :  Plusieurs présumés braqueurs interpellés par les forces de sécurité à Haraze-Mangueigne
Pour sa part, le procureur de la République près le Tribunal de grande instance de Faya, Mahamat Idriss Khamis, a assuré que les deux mis en cause répondraient des faits qui leur sont reprochés devant la loi.
La cérémonie s’est déroulée en présence de plusieurs responsables civils et militaires de la province. Les deux suspects ont été remis à la justice afin que les procédures judiciaires suivent leur cours.

items.title: Climat : la COP31 s’achève sur un échec historique à Antalya

original_payload.original_title: Climat : la COP31 s’achève sur un échec historique à Antalya
original_payload.original_body:
La conférence de l’ONU sur le climat a pris fin dimanche 22 novembre en Turquie sans aucun accord. En cause : un projet de texte final jugé inacceptable par l’Union européenne et la Suisse en raison de l’absence de référence explicite aux énergies fossiles. C’est un revers majeur pour la diplomatie climatique internationale.
Après plus de deux semaines d’âpres négociations et un record de 49 heures de prolongations — faisant de cette édition la plus longue de l’histoire des conférences onusiennes —, la COP31 s’est clôturée sur un constat d’échec dimanche 22 novembre à Antalya, en Turquie.
Lors de la séance plénière de clôture, le président turc du Sommet, Murat Kurum, a dû se résoudre à entériner l’absence de consensus. « Il est clair que certaines parties, dans cette salle, s’opposent à ce texte. Nous constatons qu’il n’existe pas de consensus sur ce document. Par conséquent, ces décisions n’ont pas été adoptées », a-t-il déclaré devant des délégations épuisées.
Lire aussi :  ‎Incendies dans les oasis : le ministère de l’Environnement tire la sonnette d’alarme
Le point de rupture s’est cristallisé autour du projet de décision finale, préparé conjointement par la Turquie et l’Australie. Le document a provoqué une levée de boucliers immédiate en omettant toute mention explicite des énergies fossiles (pétrole, gaz, charbon), pourtant responsables de l’essentiel du réchauffement climatique.
Face à ce recul jugé inacceptable, l’Union européenne, la Suisse ainsi que plusieurs autres pays ont catégoriquement rejeté le texte. À l’issue de cette clôture sans résultat, le secrétaire général de l’ONU, António Guterres, n’a pas masqué son amertume face à l’incapacité des États à s’entendre.
Lire aussi :  Lutte contre le réchauffement climatique : un réseau de contrôle des gaz à effet de serre est créé
Se disant « profondément déçu », il a tenu à adresser un message de soutien à la société civile : « Je partage la profonde frustration de tous ceux qui espéraient que les gouvernements seraient à la hauteur de ce qu’exige la crise climatique. »

items.title: Nigeria : 37 terroristes abattus par l'armée de l'air

original_payload.original_title: Nigeria : 37 terroristes abattus par l'armée de l'air
original_payload.original_body:
Afrique
Nigeria : 37 terroristes abattus par l'armée de l'air
Entre le 16 et le 23 novembre 2026, l'opération Hadin Kai a mené une série de frappes aériennes précises dans le nord-est du Nigeria, neutralisant 37 terroristes et détruisant plusieurs véhicules logistiques.
Alwihda Info
23 nov. 2026
© HQ/A
Entre le 16 et le 23 novembre 2026, l'opération Hadin Kai, menée par la Joint Task Force (North East), a intensifié sa pression sur les groupes armés dans le nord-est du Nigeria. Selon un bilan officiel, six frappes aériennes ciblées, menées sur cinq sites différents grâce à des renseignements confirmés, ont permis de neutraliser 37 terroristes.
Les opérations ont ciblé des mouvements, des cachettes et des infrastructures logistiques dans les régions de Monguno, Kerenoa et Fage, situées dans la zone de gouvernement local (LGA) de Marte.
Dès le 16 novembre, une frappe préemptive, validée par des données de surveillance et confirmée par une évaluation des dégâts de combat (BDA), a mis hors d'état de marche 10 combattants. Le lendemain, un véhicule transportant des explosifs a été détruit à Arina Chiki grâce à un suivi par système de reconnaissance (ISR).
Les actions se sont poursuivies le 23 novembre dans la zone générale de Tumbuma Baba. Un premier véhicule repéré a été détruit par une frappe aérienne. Deux suspects ayant quitté les lieux ont ensuite été suivis jusqu'à un regroupement sous un arbre réunissant huit individus au total. Une frappe coordonnée sur cette position a entraîné la neutralisation de l'ensemble du groupe, sans mouvement ultérieur détecté sur zone.
Dans son communiqué, le commandement de l'opération Hadin Kai salue le professionnalisme de ses équipes de renseignement et réaffirme sa volonté de poursuivre ces offensives en synergie avec les forces terrestres. L'objectif affiché reste la restauration d'une paix durable et la sécurisation des activités socio-économiques dans la région, tout en appelant la population à continuer de transmettre des informations jugées utiles.
