items.title: Sommet quadripartite d’Oyo : Kinshasa et Nairobi scellent un accord d'apaisement

original_payload.original_title: Sommet quadripartite d’Oyo : Kinshasa et Nairobi scellent un accord d'apaisement
original_payload.original_body:
Afrique
Sommet quadripartite d’Oyo : Kinshasa et Nairobi  scellent un accord d'apaisement
Alwihda Info
23 nov. 2026
© Les 4 chefs d'Etat autour de la table.
Par Mvouanzi Jonas
A l’initiative du président congolais Denis Sassou N’Guesso, la République Démocratique du Congo (RDC) et le Kenya ont scellé un accord d’apaisement, le 22 novembre 2026 à Oyo, en République du Congo. L’acte de paix a été conclu en présence du dirigeant togolais Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé, médiateur de l’Union africaine (UA) pour la crise sécuritaire dans l’Est congolais.
C’est une étape décisive vers la désescalade diplomatique qu’ont franchie les chefs d’État Félix-Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo de la RDC et William Samoei Ruto du Kenya. Après quelques tensions entre les deux pays, le conclave quadripartite d’Oyo a permis d’aplanir les différends dans un climat décrit comme franc et fraternel. L’avancée la plus tangible de cette rencontre réside dans la décision prise par Kinshasa et Nairobi de rétablir leurs ambassadeurs respectifs, actant ainsi la reprise normale de leurs relations bilatérales.
Les présidents Tshisekedi et Ruto ont solennellement réaffirmé leur adhésion aux principes cardinaux de la Charte de l’Union africaine : le respect mutuel de la souveraineté, l’intégrité territoriale, la non-ingérence dans les affaires intérieures et le règlement pacifique des litiges. Pour éviter toute nouvelle crispation, les deux dirigeants entendent désormais privilégier la concertation permanente et s’appuyer sur les cadres sous-régionaux existants, à savoir la Communauté d’Afrique de l’Est (CAE) et la Conférence internationale sur la région des Grands Lacs (CIRGL).
Relance économique et front commun contre Ebola
Au-delà de la résolution de la crise diplomatique entre les deux pays, le sommet d’Oyo a fixé une feuille de route axée sur des priorités concrètes. Les deux dirigeants se sont engagés à traduire ce regain de confiance par une intensification de leur coopération économique et commerciale.
Préoccupés par l’ampleur de l’épidémie d’Ebola, Félix Tshisekedi et William Ruto ont appelé à une mobilisation collective et à une coordination renforcée entre les États de la région afin d’endiguer et d’éradiquer le virus.
Ce rapprochement illustre la mise en œuvre du principe des « solutions africaines aux problèmes africains ». Les présidents de la RDC) et du Kénya ont exprimé leur profonde gratitude envers Denis Sassou N’Guesso pour sa facilitation et son hospitalité, ainsi qu’envers Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé, dont le rôle de médiateur de l’UA a été salué comme déterminant pour créer les conditions de ce dialogue.

items.title: Tchad : 20 km de voirie urbaine à bitumer en 2027 à Abéché, les acteurs locaux mobilisés

original_payload.original_title: Tchad : 20 km de voirie urbaine à bitumer en 2027 à Abéché, les acteurs locaux mobilisés
original_payload.original_body:
Tchad
Tchad : 20 km de voirie urbaine à bitumer en 2027 à Abéché, les acteurs locaux mobilisés
À Abéché, les autorités locales et les représentants citoyens se sont mobilisés pour identifier les axes prioritaires du futur projet de bitumage de 20 km de voirie prévu en 2027.
Alwihda Info
23 nov. 2026
Par Hambali Nassour Ourada
Le président du Conseil provincial du Ouaddaï, Mahamat Ali Rahama, et le maire de la commune d’Abéché, Dr Abdel-Mahmoud Adam Yaya, ont coprésidé, ce lundi 23 novembre 2026, une rencontre de concertation consacrée à l'identification des axes prioritaires du projet de bitumage de 20 km de voirie urbaine prévu pour 2027.
Annoncé par le président de la République lors de sa dernière visite dans la ville, ce projet a réuni les conseillers municipaux, les administrateurs délégués des arrondissements, les responsables techniques, les membres du cadre de concertation communal et de la consultation citoyenne, ainsi que des représentants d'ONG et des associations de quartiers.
À l'ouverture des travaux, le maire Dr Abdel-Mahmoud Adam Yaya a annoncé l'arrivée prochaine d'une commission technique chargée du projet. Il a insisté sur l'importance de cette concertation pour recueillir les propositions locales et faciliter le ciblage des artères stratégiques.
Pour sa part, le président du Conseil provincial du Ouaddaï, Mahamat Ali Rahama, a salué cette dynamique collaborative. Il a invité les participants à formuler des recommandations rigoureuses au regard de l'impact structurant de ce chantier pour le développement d'Abéché.
Durant les échanges, plusieurs pistes ont été avancées. De nombreux intervenants ont plaidé pour l'aménagement de grands axes reliant l'Est à l'Ouest et le Sud au Nord, avec pour objectif de désengorger la circulation et de fluidifier le trafic urbain.
Au terme de la réunion, une commission ad hoc a été mise sur pied afin de mener une descente sur le terrain et d'évaluer la faisabilité des propositions retenues.
Cette démarche participative doit garantir la sélection d'itinéraires adaptés aux besoins réels de la population, contribuant ainsi à moderniser durablement les infrastructures routières de la cité.

items.title: CEDEAO : les chefs d'état-major valident le calendrier de déploiement de la force anti-terroriste pour 2027

original_payload.original_title: CEDEAO : les chefs d'état-major valident le calendrier de déploiement de la force anti-terroriste pour 2027
original_payload.original_body:
Afrique
CEDEAO : les chefs d'état-major valident le calendrier de déploiement de la force anti-terroriste pour 2027
Réunis à Dakar, les chefs d'état-major de la CEDEAO ont validé une feuille de route pour déployer d'ici décembre 2027 une force régionale dédiée à la lutte contre le terrorisme.
Alwihda Info
23 nov. 2026
© DR
La Communauté économique des États de l'Afrique de l'Ouest (CEDEAO) a franchi une nouvelle étape dans son architecture de sécurité. Les États membres se sont accordés sur une feuille de route pour concrétiser le déploiement de sa Force de lutte contre le terrorisme d'ici décembre 2027.
Cette décision constitue le principal acquis de la 45e réunion ordinaire du Comité des chefs d'état-major de la CEDEAO (CCDS), organisée à Dakar, au Sénégal, du 17 au 19 novembre 2026.
Durant trois jours, les responsables militaires de la région ont analysé la situation sécuritaire et harmonisé leurs réponses face à l'expansion du terrorisme, de l'extrémisme violent, de la criminalité organisée transnationale et des menaces maritimes.

items.title: Investigation underway into cause of Zanzibar hotel blaze

original_payload.original_body:
Tanzania
Investigations are ongoing into the cause of a huge fire that engulfed six hotels along a popular beach in Zanzibar.
The blaze broke out on Saturday afternoon at Makofi Hotel on  Nungwi beach  at the northern end of the island. Fuelled by strong winds and thatched roofs, it rapidly spread to neighbouring properties.
Firefighters battled for three hours to bring the fire under control. Several hotel workers were injured and around 180 tourists evacuated.
original_payload.original_summary: Investigations continued Monday into the cause of a huge fire that engulfed six hotels along a popular beach in Tanzania ’s semiautonomous archipelago of Zanzibar. Several hotel workers were injured in the blaze over the weekend. Authorities said about 180 tourists were safely evacuated.

items.title: AI giant Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after spy scandal

original_payload.original_title: AI giant Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after spy scandal
original_payload.original_body:
USA
Nvidia on Monday reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive in a stunning reversal that the company said followed input from  "senior levels"  of the US government.
Huang   resigned two weeks ago   over an affair with a woman whom US intelligence agencies suspect of spying for China, a departure that sent Wall Street tumbling and stoked fears for a US economy reliant on the AI investment boom.
US stocks bounced early Monday after the news emerged, with Nvidia rocketing about 26% and the tech-heavy Nasdaq up more than 5%.

Les commissions des finances et des lois se réuniront le 24 novembre pour examiner les suites du décret budgétaire présidentiel contesté au Parlement.

L’Assemblée nationale du Sénégal a convoqué pour mardi 24 novembre 2026 une réunion commune de ses commissions des finances et des lois afin d’examiner une proposition de résolution portant sur le décret qui a mis en vigueur le budget rectificatif de 2026. La convocation, datée du lundi 23 novembre, intervient après le rejet de ce projet budgétaire par les députés.
Le document est signé par Alphonse Mané Sambou, président de la Commission des finances et du contrôle budgétaire. Il réunit les membres de cette commission et ceux de la Commission des lois, de la décentralisation, du travail et des droits humains. L’ordre du jour vise expressément le décret n° 2026-2416 du 19 novembre et les responsabilités liées à son exécution.
Quatre jours plus tôt, le président Bassirou Diomaye Faye avait  annoncé la mise en vigueur  du projet de loi de finances rectificative malgré son rejet à l’Assemblée. Le communiqué présidentiel du 19 novembre, signé par le ministre secrétaire général de la Présidence Oumar Samba Ba, invoquait la continuité de l’État et le fonctionnement régulier des pouvoirs publics.
Le  rapport accompagnant le décret  fait référence à l’article 68 de la Constitution sénégalaise. Celui-ci accorde au Parlement un délai de soixante jours pour voter les projets de loi de finances et prévoit, dans les conditions qu’il fixe, leur mise en vigueur par décret à l’expiration de ce délai. Le projet rectificatif avait été transmis à l’Assemblée le 18 septembre 2026.
Les députés avaient repoussé le texte en commission les 23 et 30 octobre, puis en séance plénière le 3 novembre.  Le décompte corrigé de ce dernier vote  faisait état de 126 voix favorables au rejet. Le gouvernement a présenté le recours au décret comme un moyen d’assurer la continuité budgétaire et le respect des engagements de l’État.
La proposition de résolution porte désormais le différend sur le terrain parlementaire, autour du recours à cette procédure et des responsabilités découlant de son application. Les deux commissions sont convoquées mardi 24 novembre à 10 heures dans la salle Marie Joséphine Diallo, au nouveau bâtiment de l’Assemblée nationale à Dakar.

Pete Edochie a affirmé que son fils Yul avait subi un rejet professionnel après la controverse née de son second mariage avec l’actrice Judy Austin. Dans un extrait de l’émission  Unfiltered With Ugo and Precious , diffusé dimanche 22 novembre, le vétéran de Nollywood assure que cette hostilité a gagné certaines cérémonies de récompenses.
Selon lui, des organisateurs ont cessé de retenir Yul Edochie dans leurs sélections. Pete Edochie n’a toutefois cité ni cérémonie, ni organisateur, ni période précise pour étayer cette accusation.
« Chaque fois que des prix sont organisés, ils ne l’incluent pas », a-t-il déclaré.
L’acteur de 79 ans a également décrit son fils comme un homme résistant, resté concentré sur sa carrière malgré les critiques. Il a salué le fait que Yul n’ait pas publiquement attaqué May Edochie, sa première épouse, pendant leur conflit conjugal.
La polémique remonte à avril 2022, lorsque Yul Edochie a annoncé la naissance d’un fils avec Judy Austin et présenté l’actrice comme sa seconde épouse. Il était alors marié à May Edochie, avec qui il avait quatre enfants. La même année,  il avait défendu publiquement sa décision  face aux critiques.
May Edochie, qui avait rejeté l’idée d’un mariage polygame, a engagé une procédure de divorce en août 2023. Pete Edochie avait déclaré cette année-là ne pas avoir été informé à l’avance du second mariage de son fils. L’entretien complet avec le vétéran doit être mis en ligne mercredi.

Le Conseil du Café-Cacao (CCC) a refusé le déchargement de 3 765 tonnes de fèves proposées dans le cadre d’une opération de reprise des stocks ivoiriens. Dans une  note datée du 20 novembre 2026 , rendue publique ce lundi 23 novembre, le régulateur invoque une fraude sur le grainage. L’opération a permis de réceptionner 96 235 tonnes sur les 100 000 autorisées par le gouvernement.
Le décompte distingue 35 011 tonnes déchargées directement par le Conseil du Café-Cacao et 61 224 tonnes traitées par l’Organisation interprofessionnelle agricole de la filière café-cacao (OIA-CC). Ce second volume comprend 955 tonnes prises en charge pour le compte du Syndicat national agricole pour le progrès en Côte d’Ivoire (SYNAPCI). Les 3 765 tonnes refusées n’entrent pas dans les volumes réceptionnés.
Pour financer l’opération, l’État ivoirien avait mis à disposition une enveloppe de 280 milliards de FCFA. Le CCC fait état de 269 457 683 600 FCFA dépensés, soit environ 96,2 % du budget prévu. La différence entre l’allocation initiale et les décaissements déclarés atteint 10,54 milliards de FCFA.
Cette intervention répondait au ralentissement des achats de cacao constaté en décembre 2025, pendant la campagne principale 2025-2026. Un inventaire réalisé du 14 au 18 janvier 2026 avait recensé 123 000 tonnes détenues par les sociétés coopératives. Le gouvernement avait ensuite autorisé l’enlèvement de 100 000 tonnes de ce stock.
Au 11 février, le Conseil du Café-Cacao avait lui-même déchargé 35 011 tonnes. L’interprofession avait alors été associée au dispositif pour prendre en charge le reste. L’achèvement de l’opération avait été annoncé le 5 août, avant la publication du bilan détaillé de novembre.
Les sociétés coopératives peuvent consulter la liste définitive des bénéficiaires auprès des treize délégations régionales du Conseil du Café-Cacao, ainsi que sur ses plateformes institutionnelles.

La gendarmerie sénégalaise a intercepté 101 candidats à l’émigration irrégulière samedi 21 novembre 2026, dans les bolongs de Mar Loth, sur le territoire de Fimela, dans la région de Fatick. L’opération, rendue publique lundi 23 novembre, a également conduit à la saisie d’une pirogue de 17 mètres et de 108 bidons destinés à son approvisionnement en carburant.
Le groupe était composé de 93 hommes et de huit femmes. Deux enfants figuraient parmi les personnes interceptées. Les personnes interceptées comprenaient 26 ressortissants guinéens et un Malien, selon le bilan communiqué par les forces de sécurité sénégalaises.
L’intervention a été menée par la brigade territoriale de Fimela, appuyée par des éléments de la section environnement et de l’Escadron de surveillance et d’intervention de Fatick. Les bidons saisis ont chacun une capacité de 25 litres, soit une capacité totale de 2 700 litres.
Les personnes interceptées et le matériel saisi ont été mis à la disposition de la brigade de Fimela. Une enquête est en cours pour établir les circonstances de la tentative de départ et identifier ses éventuels organisateurs.
Le delta du Saloum avait déjà été le théâtre de plusieurs interceptions en octobre. Dans la région de Fatick, 378 candidats à l’émigration irrégulière avaient été arrêtés au cours de trois opérations menées du 20 au 22 octobre 2026. Le dernier jour, 208 personnes avaient été interceptées dans le bolong de l’Iranne, près de l’île de Bassoul, avec la saisie de trois pirogues, de moteurs hors-bord et de 5 800 litres de carburant.
Ces opérations conduites avant les départs s’ajoutent aux interventions en mer. Entre le 19 et le 21 novembre, la Marine nationale sénégalaise a annoncé avoir  secouru 1 007 personnes lors d’opérations distinctes , dont 946 à bord de sept pirogues prises en charge au large du pays.

L’ancien international saoudien Hussein Abdulghani a vivement contesté l’impact actuel de Cristiano Ronaldo à Al-Nassr après la défaite 3-1 face à Al-Ahli, vendredi 20 novembre à Djeddah. Invité de l’émission « Nadeena » sur MBC1, il estime que le Portugais ne compense plus par son influence dans le jeu les buts qu’il continue d’inscrire.
« Ronaldo est un grand joueur, mais il ne peut plus faire la différence », a déclaré l’ancien défenseur, qui considère le capitaine d’Al-Nassr comme un « fardeau » sur le reste de la rencontre. Abdulghani a insisté sur la nécessité, pour un attaquant, de participer à la construction du jeu et pas seulement de conclure les actions.
Face à Mohamed Noor, autre ancienne figure du football saoudien, il a aussi mis en cause l’intérêt collectif de la course aux 1 000 buts. À la question de savoir s’il souhaiterait voir Ronaldo à Al-Ittihad, Noor a répondu par la négative, tout en reconnaissant son efficacité devant le but.
La prestation contre Al-Ahli a nourri cette critique. Ronaldo a ouvert le score à la 14e minute, avant d’envoyer un penalty sur le poteau quatre minutes plus tard. Al-Ahli a ensuite renversé la rencontre grâce à Galeno, Ivan Toney sur penalty et Roger Ibañez.
Le quintuple Ballon d’Or totalise 986 buts en carrière, selon le décompte mentionné lors de ce débat. Il lui en manque quatorze pour atteindre la barre symbolique des 1 000.

Selon l’UEFA, 46 % des passes décisives en jeu ouvert sont venues de l’axe lors de la quatrième journée de Ligue des champions.
Europe Sport      Par  Henry DONCHE
·   23 Nov. 2026 à 16:49  23/11/26 16:49       ·   3 min  de lecture
Mis à jour le  23 novembre 2026 à 17:25
Lire hors-ligne
Écouter

Côme face au RB Leipzig le 10 septembre 2026 (archives). Photo : Richibrics / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0. Image recadrée et convertie en WebP.
Partager
Ajouter Bénin Web TV à vos sources préférées
Près d’une passe décisive sur deux réalisée dans le jeu lors de la quatrième journée de la Ligue des champions est venue des zones centrales. L’UEFA chiffre cette proportion à 46 % dans une  analyse tactique publiée lundi 23 novembre , à la veille de la reprise de la compétition. Ce chiffre concerne cette seule journée et les actions de jeu ouvert, sans les coups de pied arrêtés.
Côme figure au premier rang des équipes qui exploitent ces espaces. Le club italien a marqué 19 buts lors de ses quatre premières rencontres européennes, un record pour un débutant dans cette compétition. Son meneur argentin Nico Paz a participé directement à huit de ces réalisations, avec trois buts et cinq passes décisives. Ces cinq dernières font de lui le meilleur passeur du tournoi après quatre journées.
La démonstration la plus spectaculaire est intervenue le 4 novembre, avec une  victoire 9-1 sur le terrain de Lens . Les observateurs techniques de l’UEFA, Ernesto Valverde et Steve Cooper, ont notamment examiné les déplacements des joueurs de Côme sur les actions impliquant Lucas Da Cunha, Nico Paz et Tasos Douvikas.
L’enjeu n’est pas simplement d’accumuler des joueurs dans l’axe. Côme attire d’abord l’adversaire vers une zone, puis accélère le jeu après avoir franchi une ligne défensive. Le mouvement de Paz entre le milieu et la défense lui permet de recevoir face au but ou de servir Douvikas. Sur une autre action étudiée, lors de Leipzig–Manchester City, la défense se resserre sur un joueur qui rentre dans l’axe et libère ainsi un couloir extérieur pour Antonio Nusa.
Cette articulation entre l’intérieur et les côtés donne un sens concret au chiffre avancé par l’UEFA. La passe décisive peut venir du centre, mais les déplacements sur les ailes contribuent aussi à y créer de l’espace. Les données ne disent pas que l’axe est la seule manière de marquer. Elles décrivent la provenance des dernières passes durant la quatrième journée.
Le prochain examen de cette efficacité aura lieu mardi 24 novembre, lorsque Côme recevra l’AEK Athènes à 21 heures, heure de Cotonou. Douvikas a marqué lors de chacun de ses quatre premiers matchs de Ligue des champions. L’AEK n’a encore jamais gagné à l’extérieur dans cette compétition, après cinq nuls et douze défaites.  Les 19 buts inscrits par les Italiens  placent leur animation offensive au centre de cette rencontre.

Le Ghana a remporté pour la première fois la Coupe du monde de football pour amputés en battant le Maroc 1-0, dimanche 22 novembre à San Juan de los Lagos, au Mexique. Les Black Challenge concluent ainsi un tournoi de 24 équipes par un sacre inédit.
Le capitaine Richard Opentil a inscrit l’unique but de la finale à la 32e minute. La sélection ghanéenne a ensuite préservé son avantage face à un adversaire qu’elle avait déjà battu lors de la finale de la Coupe d’Afrique 2024.
Ce titre fait du Ghana le deuxième pays africain champion du monde de la discipline, après l’Angola en 2018. Les Black Challenge prolongent une série continentale qui comprend également leur victoire aux Jeux para-africains de 2023.
Le parcours à élimination directe a mené le Ghana devant les États-Unis, battus 3-1 en huitièmes de finale, puis l’Égypte, dominée 2-0 en quarts. En demi-finale, les Ghanéens ont éliminé la Turquie 4-3 aux tirs au but après un nul 1-1.
L’attaquant Mubarik Mohammed a terminé meilleur buteur du tournoi avec sept réalisations. La compétition s’est déroulée du 13 au 22 novembre au Mexique.

Une mission de la Commission de consolidation de la paix des Nations unies est annoncée à Abidjan les 23 et 24 novembre 2026 pour examiner, avec la Banque africaine de développement (BAD), les moyens de mieux financer la prévention des conflits en Afrique. Selon les informations publiées lundi par KOACI, la délégation doit comprendre Omar Hilale, président de cette commission et représentant permanent du Maroc auprès de l’ONU, ainsi qu’Elizabeth Spehar, sous-secrétaire générale des Nations unies chargée de la consolidation de la paix.
Le programme annoncé comprend des échanges avec le gouvernement ivoirien, l’équipe des Nations unies en Côte d’Ivoire, la société civile et des représentants du secteur privé. Les discussions doivent porter sur l’articulation entre engagements politiques, investissements de développement et renforcement de la résilience dans les pays confrontés aux risques de conflit.
Cette visite intervient un mois après la neuvième réunion consultative entre la Commission de consolidation de la paix et le Conseil de paix et de sécurité de l’Union africaine. Le  communiqué conjoint du 22 octobre  mettait l’accent sur une coopération régionale appuyée sur les priorités des États africains, notamment dans la prévention et la reconstruction après les conflits.
La BAD a fait du financement de la résilience l’un de ses axes de travail. Le 17 novembre, elle a annoncé un  plan d’action conjoint avec le Comité international de la Croix-Rouge pour 2026-2028 , destiné à étendre les interventions dans les pays touchés par les conflits et la fragilité.
Cette coopération prévoit notamment des actions dans l’accès à l’eau et à la santé, la sécurité alimentaire et les moyens de subsistance des populations. L’accord s’appuie sur les capacités de financement et de dialogue de la banque, ainsi que sur la présence humanitaire du CICR dans les territoires concernés.

Manchester City recevra Naples sans Antoine Semenyo, mardi 24 novembre, lors de la cinquième journée de Ligue des champions. L’ailier international ghanéen poursuit sa rééducation et devrait manquer encore plusieurs semaines de compétition. Son entraîneur Enzo Maresca a, en revanche, confirmé lundi le retour de Matheus Nunes pour cette rencontre européenne.
Le technicien italien a présenté Semenyo comme le seul forfait certain de son effectif. Nunes, absent lors du match nul contre Fulham (1-1) samedi en Premier League, est à nouveau disponible. Le staff doit encore évaluer l’état physique d’autres joueurs après la dernière séance d’entraînement, a indiqué  Manchester City .
Semenyo s’est blessé lors de la victoire contre Ipswich à la mi-octobre. Son indisponibilité prive City d’une option offensive supplémentaire face au club italien, sans qu’une date précise de reprise ait été annoncée. Le retour de Nunes offre à Maresca une solution de plus sur le côté droit, où Abdukodir Khusanov avait été utilisé pendant son absence.
En Ligue des champions, Manchester City occupe la septième place avec neuf points après quatre rencontres, tandis que Naples est vingt-septième avec trois points. Les huit premiers de la phase de ligue se qualifient directement pour les huitièmes de finale. Les équipes classées de la neuvième à la vingt-quatrième place doivent passer par des barrages.
Le coup d’envoi est fixé à 20 heures à Manchester, soit  21 heures à Cotonou . Avant le déplacement à l’Etihad Stadium,  Massimiliano Allegri a identifié les prochaines rencontres de Naples  contre Bruges, Sabah et Viking comme déterminantes pour ses chances de qualification.

Teddy Riner a déposé plainte après les propos d’Emmanuelle Mignon, qui avait comparé sa première visite de campagne dans un hôpital de Saint-Denis à « Tintin au Congo », a rapporté BFMTV lundi 23 novembre. Cette démarche judiciaire constitue un nouveau développement dans la polémique née neuf jours plus tôt.
L’ancienne directrice de cabinet de Nicolas Sarkozy avait prononcé cette formule le 14 novembre sur France Inter, au lendemain d’un déplacement du judoka à l’hôpital Delafontaine. Elle avait alors critiqué les débuts de campagne du quintuple champion olympique.
Interrogée sur le sens de sa comparaison, Emmanuelle Mignon avait expliqué qu’elle voulait décrire un candidat découvrant un nouvel univers. La référence à l’album publié en 1931 avait suscité des réactions en raison de ses représentations coloniales et de ses stéréotypes sur l’Afrique.
Teddy Riner avait passé près de trois heures dans l’établissement de Seine-Saint-Denis le 13 novembre. Il y avait rencontré des soignants et échangé sur leurs conditions de travail avant d’annoncer la poursuite de ses déplacements de terrain.
Le champion de 37 ans a annoncé le 9 novembre sa candidature à l’élection présidentielle française de 2027. Depuis cette entrée en campagne, il s’est présenté comme un candidat indépendant des partis et a indiqué qu’il dévoilerait progressivement son équipe et son programme.

original_payload.original_body:
Donald Trump (Rawpixel)

23/11/2026    par    Gildas Amoussou

Lundi 23 novembre 2026 à Berlin, le secrétaire général de  l’OTAN ,  Mark Rutte , a appelé les Européens à réduire leur dépendance militaire envers les  États-Unis . Il a estimé que cette situation ne pouvait durer indéfiniment.  « À long terme, ce n’est pas viable  », a-t-il prévenu lors de son intervention à l’ouverture de l’Assemblée parlementaire de l’Alliance.
Pour rappel, les  États-Unis  disposent d’environ 450 avions-ravitailleurs, contre 156 en  Europe , et dominent le transport stratégique avec plus de 200 C-17. Ils fournissent l’essentiel des satellites et du renseignement électromagnétique de l’Alliance, ainsi que la majeure partie de la défense antimissile de ses membres européens.   Rutte   qualifie leur parapluie de  « garant ultime de notre liberté ».
Rutte pointe un déséquilibre
Le responsable a déclaré : «  Il est tout de même étrange que, avec 600 millions de personnes vivant sur le territoire européen de l’OTAN, nous soyons aussi dépendants d’un pays situé à huit heures de vol, qui compte 340 millions d’habitants, pour nous défendre contre 140 millions de Russes  ».
Mark Rutte  estime ainsi que les Européens doivent assumer une responsabilité dans leur sécurité. Son avertissement intervient alors que la Russie poursuit le renforcement de ses capacités militaires et que les membres de l’Alliance sont appelés à investir davantage dans leur défense

items.title: Governo absorve maior bolo no crédito para gerir dívida pública

original_payload.original_title: Governo absorve maior bolo no crédito para gerir dívida pública
original_payload.original_body:
A ministra das Finanças, Carla Louveira, justifica a maior absorção do crédito bancário pelo Governo, em detrimento do sector privado, com a necessidade de equilibrar a dívida pública interna e externa. A governante explica que o recurso ao financiamento interno resulta das mudanças na arquitectura financeira internacional e da redução das oportunidades de financiamento externo.
Recentemente, o sector privado manifestou preocupação com a crescente absorção do crédito à economia pelo Governo, que, durante o terceiro trimestre deste ano, terá recorrido ao financiamento bancário em mais do dobro do volume destinado às empresas, situação que, segundo os empresários, compromete a capacidade de financiamento e a sobrevivência dos negócios.
Em reacção às preocupações, Carla Louveira afirma que o recurso ao mercado financeiro nacional faz parte de uma estratégia de gestão da dívida pública, que procura equilibrar as fontes de financiamento do Estado.
“Os parceiros financeiros internacionais têm mais demanda por outras prioridades de investimento, tanto ao nível internacional, como também numa abordagem de ganhos mútuos em termos daquilo que vão financiar nas economias beneficiárias”, explicou a ministra.
A governante reconhece que o endividamento interno tem aumentado nos últimos anos, mas considera que esta opção permite responder às necessidades de financiamento do Estado e equilibrar as carteiras da dívida pública.
“O principal objectivo é mesmo estabilizar e equilibrar as duas carteiras, externa e interna”, sublinhou Carla Louveira, acrescentando que o Governo tem recorrido a instrumentos como Bilhetes e Obrigações do Tesouro para mobilizar recursos no mercado nacional.
Sobre as dívidas do Estado com os funcionários públicos, particularmente os professores, a ministra assegura que o Executivo está a implementar uma estratégia de amortização progressiva dos valores em atraso.
“A dívida acumulada aos professores é uma das dívidas que nós temos, portanto, temos que responder de forma cumulativa às dívidas”, afirmou, reconhecendo que o montante em causa é significativo.
Quanto ao sector da Saúde, Carla Louveira considera que o processo de regularização está praticamente concluído, embora ainda existam valores residuais por pagar.
“Estamos a fechar relativamente ao passado da dívida da Saúde. Praticamente, já não temos”, declarou, acrescentando que o pagamento das horas extraordinárias correntes daquele sector está actualizado desde Junho de 2025.
Na Educação, a governante explica que a dívida acumulada está relacionada, entre outros factores, com a implementação da Tabela Salarial Única e a manutenção da fórmula de cálculo das horas extraordinárias.
Carla Louveira falava esta segunda-feira, em Maputo, à margem da visita do Presidente da República, Daniel Chapo, ao Banco de Moçambique.

items.title: Acidentes com mototaxistas caem de cinco por semana para dois por mês em Inhambane

original_payload.original_title: Acidentes com mototaxistas caem de cinco por semana para dois por mês em Inhambane
original_payload.original_body:
O Conselho Municipal de Inhambane reforçou a fiscalização aos mototaxistas e aposta na formação obrigatória dos operadores para retirar das estradas condutores sem habilitação legal. As autoridades municipais afirmam que as medidas já estão a produzir resultados, com uma redução dos acidentes de viação, que anteriormente chegavam a quatro ou cinco por semana e agora variam entre um e dois por mês.
A cidade de Inhambane está a registar uma redução dos acidentes de viação envolvendo mototaxistas, numa altura em que o Conselho Municipal intensifica a fiscalização e a formação dos operadores, com o objectivo de impedir que pessoas sem habilitação legal continuem a exercer a actividade nas estradas.
Segundo o vereador dos Transportes no Conselho Municipal de Inhambane, Novais Abubacar, a edilidade decidiu reforçar as medidas de controlo perante a preocupação com o número de acidentes envolvendo motociclos utilizados no transporte de passageiros.
A estratégia municipal passa por garantir que os mototaxistas recebam formação teórica e prática, conheçam as regras de circulação rodoviária e obtenham a licença de condução antes de começarem a transportar passageiros.
Para Novais Abubacar, o exercício da actividade deve obedecer às exigências estabelecidas no Código da Estrada, uma vez que a circulação de condutores sem habilitação representa um risco para os passageiros e para os restantes utentes da via pública.
“O critério é participar na formação, obter a licença de condução e, nessa formação, inclui-se a teoria e a prática. É assim como o Código da Estrada recomenda. Não se pode ir à via pública com um meio circulante sem que tenha licença ou algum documento que lhe dê o direito de conduzir”, explicou o vereador.
O responsável acrescentou que o município pretende assegurar que os operadores estejam devidamente preparados para enfrentar as exigências da circulação rodoviária, evitando que a actividade seja exercida por pessoas sem conhecimentos suficientes sobre as regras de trânsito.
A formação dos mototaxistas tem sido acompanhada por acções de sensibilização e fiscalização, numa tentativa de reduzir os comportamentos de risco e melhorar a segurança nas estradas da cidade.
De acordo com Novais Abubacar, os primeiros resultados são encorajadores. O município afirma que os acidentes envolvendo mototaxistas, que anteriormente chegavam a quatro ou cinco por semana, passaram a ocorrer com uma frequência de apenas um ou dois por mês.
“A nossa cidade agora está a respirar um pouco de alívio em relação aos acidentes. Isso é resultado dessas formações e da sensibilização que temos feito para consciencializar os jovens sobre a necessidade de estarem habilitados à condução desses meios”, afirmou.
O vereador considera que a redução dos sinistros demonstra a importância de combinar a fiscalização com a formação dos operadores, embora reconheça que o objectivo das autoridades municipais é diminuir ainda mais a ocorrência de acidentes.
“Nós registávamos semanalmente quatro a cinco acidentes e, finalmente, hoje estamos a registar um ou dois acidentes mensalmente, mas a ideia é mesmo eliminarmos todos os acidentes possíveis”, declarou.
Os números apresentados pelo município representam uma redução expressiva na frequência dos acidentes reportados, embora não tenham sido indicados os períodos exactos de comparação nem o número de mototaxistas abrangidos pelas formações e acções de fiscalização.
A preocupação com a sinistralidade envolvendo mototaxistas não se limita à cidade de Inhambane. Na vizinha cidade da Maxixe, por exemplo, chegaram a ser registados mais de 12 acidentes de viação em apenas 20 dias, uma situação que demonstra a dimensão do problema na província.
Para o Conselho Municipal de Inhambane, a prioridade é consolidar os resultados alcançados, mantendo a fiscalização e a exigência de habilitação legal para o exercício da actividade.
A edilidade pretende, desta forma, reduzir a circulação de condutores sem formação e garantir maior segurança aos passageiros que diariamente recorrem aos mototáxis como meio de transporte.

items.title: El Niño ameaça 2,2 milhões de pessoas no País

original_payload.original_title: El Niño ameaça 2,2 milhões de pessoas no País
original_payload.original_body:
Um relatório internacional alerta que o El Niño pode afectar 2,22 milhões de moçambicanos, colocando o País entre os de maior risco da África Austral, com condições mais secas e quentes na época agrícola.
No capítulo dedicado à África Austral, o relatório de Actualização Global de Novembro sobre o ENOS (El Niño-Oscilação Sul) identifica Moçambique, Malawi, Zimbabwe, Zâmbia, Madagáscar e Angola como estando “entre os países de maior risco” da região.
No documento, produzido pelo Grupo de Trabalho Global sobre ENOS do Comité Permanente Interagências (IASC), mecanismo que reúne agências das Nações Unidas, organizações não-governamentais internacionais e outros parceiros humanitários para coordenar a resposta a crises provocadas pelo fenómeno climático, alerta-se que a região deverá enfrentar condições “mais secas e mais quentes do que a média”.
Este cenário, alerta, poderá afectar a produção agrícola, a disponibilidade de água e a segurança alimentar de milhões de pessoas. Em concreto, o Governo de Moçambique estima, citado no documento, que 2,22 milhões de pessoas possam ser afectadas pelos impactos do fenómeno, uma das projecções nacionais mais elevadas entre os países abrangidos pela análise regional.
O documento refere que, em Moçambique, os “planos nacionais de preparação e contingência foram actualizados”, acrescentando que o País está entre aqueles onde já foram activadas medidas antecipadas para reduzir os impactos previstos do El Niño.
Entre essas medidas contam-se acções de preparação apoiadas por agências humanitárias e parceiros internacionais, numa altura em que o relatório sublinha a necessidade de reforçar a intervenção antes do agravamento esperado das condições climáticas e humanitárias.
Assinala igualmente que o acesso humanitário continua condicionado pela insegurança em partes do Norte de Moçambique, o que poderá dificultar a prestação de assistência às populações vulneráveis caso os impactos previstos se materializem.
O relatório destaca ainda a disponibilização de dois milhões de dólares através do Fundo Humanitário de Moçambique para organizações não-governamentais nacionais desenvolverem intervenções antecipadas relacionadas com o fenómeno.
A análise conclui que as consequências humanitárias mais severas do actual episódio de El Niño na África Austral deverão tornar-se evidentes após as colheitas de Abril de 2027, prevendo-se que as necessidades atinjam o pico entre Novembro de 2027 e Março de 2028.
Além dos riscos de seca, o documento alerta que alguns países da região poderão enfrentar fenómenos extremos localizados, incluindo cheias, ciclones e surtos de doenças associados às alterações nos padrões climáticos.
Os autores alertam também para um défice acentuado de financiamento, destacando que os planos nacionais de contingência dos países da África Austral dispõem actualmente de apenas cerca de 11% dos recursos necessários para responder aos impactos esperados do fenómeno climático.
A actualização refere que o actual episódio de El Niño poderá ser um dos mais intensos já registados, com a Organização Meteorológica Mundial (OMM) a prever uma anomalia de cerca de +3,8 graus Celsius entre Novembro de 2026 e Janeiro de 2027, atingindo o pico em Dezembro e prolongando os seus efeitos até 2027.
O relatório indica ainda que temperaturas acima do normal são “muito prováveis” em grande parte do mundo pelo menos até Janeiro-Março de 2027, agravando os riscos de calor extremo, seca e precipitação intensa.
O documento assinala igualmente que a região deverá enfrentar uma época ciclónica abaixo da média, embora ressalve que um único ciclone poderá provocar impactos catastróficos.

items.title: Gueta Chapo quer líderes comunitários activos no combate à violência baseada no género

original_payload.original_title: Gueta Chapo quer líderes comunitários activos no combate à violência baseada no género
original_payload.original_body:
A Primeira-Dama da República, Gueta Chapo, defendeu, no domingo, em Pemba, província de Cabo Delgado, o envolvimento das lideranças comunitárias e religiosas no combate à violência baseada no género, considerando que estes actores são, frequentemente, os primeiros a receber pedidos de socorro de mulheres, raparigas e crianças vítimas de violência.
Gueta Chapo expressou esta posição durante o lançamento da formação de 4800 partes interessadas do programa Empodera, iniciativa que visa reforçar a prevenção e a resposta à violência baseada no género em Moçambique.
Na sua intervenção de ocasião, explicou que a formação irá abordar matérias relacionadas com a legislação de combate à violência baseada no género, uniões prematuras, retenção da rapariga na escola, prevenção e mecanismos de resposta à violência.
A iniciativa dá continuidade às acções iniciadas em 2025 nas três regiões do País e enquadra-se também na Norma Ambiental e Social 10 do Banco Mundial, relativa ao envolvimento das partes interessadas e à divulgação da informação.
A Primeira-Dama justificou a realização da iniciativa em Cabo Delgado com as características da província, onde coexistem corredores de mobilidade humana, zonas rurais de difícil acesso e comunidades onde persistem práticas nocivas aos direitos das mulheres, raparigas e crianças. Sublinhou, entretanto, que a região dispõe de lideranças, instituições e comunidades com capacidade para contribuir para a transformação desta realidade.
Gueta Chapo recordou que a igualdade de género e o empoderamento da mulher integram as prioridades do Programa Quinquenal do Governo 2025-2029, sob a liderança do Presidente da República, Daniel Francisco Chapo. Neste contexto, explicou que o Empodera abrange 63 distritos das 11 províncias do País, com a meta de alcançar directamente 250 mil mulheres e raparigas, capacitar oito mil prestadores de serviços e reforçar 50 instituições, com vista à aproximação dos serviços às comunidades.
Na província de Cabo Delgado, o programa abrange   oito distritos  , nomeadamente Ancuabe, Chiúre, Meluco, Metuge, Mueda, Namuno e Pemba, onde serão formadas 568 partes interessadas. A Primeira-Dama informou igualmente que a província acolhe cinco dos 30 Centros de Atendimento Integrado existentes no País, defendendo que estas estruturas devem constituir espaços efectivos de acolhimento e assistência às vítimas.
“Um centro de atendimento integrado não pode ser apenas um edifício. Tem de ser uma porta aberta quando todas as outras portas se fecharam”, afirmou.
A Primeira-Dama abordou a dimensão da violência doméstica, revelando que, no primeiro semestre de 2026, foram atendidos 5248 casos em todo o país, contra 4812 no período homólogo de 2025. Em Cabo Delgado, foram registados 140 casos no mesmo período.
Perante a evolução dos números, questionou a eficácia das acções de sensibilização realizadas até agora. Alertou ainda que muitos episódios de violência não chegam às autoridades, sobretudo quando familiares optam por negociações com os agressores em vez de denunciar os crimes.
Outrossim, destacou a necessidade de combater as uniões prematuras, alertando para as consequências destas práticas na saúde, na educação e no futuro das raparigas. Neste âmbito, referiu que 1208 crianças vítimas de uniões prematuras foram reunificadas com as respectivas famílias, tendo conseguido regressar à escola.
Gueta Chapo defendeu que as menores devem permanecer no sistema de ensino e ter condições para construir o próprio futuro, sublinhando que a dependência económica e a interrupção dos estudos podem contribuir para a permanência das vítimas em situações de violência.
Na ocasião, apelou às famílias, aos líderes comunitários, às instituições de ensino e às autoridades para assumirem responsabilidades na educação das crianças e na prevenção da violência, considerando que a protecção das mulheres e raparigas exige mudanças de comportamento no seio familiar e na sociedade.
“A missão não termina na punição do agressor, mas sim começa antes da violência. Ela começa na família, na escola, na comunidade”, afirmou, acrescentando que a educação deve promover o respeito entre rapazes e raparigas, dentro e fora do ambiente familiar.
A Primeira-Dama terminou defendendo que o trabalho de sensibilização deve ser contínuo e envolver todos os sectores da sociedade, de modo a garantir a protecção dos direitos das mulheres, raparigas e crianças.

items.title: Ethiopia’s Deputy PM Urges African Nations to Move Beyond Raw Material Exports, Boost Value Addition

original_payload.original_title: Ethiopia’s Deputy PM Urges African Nations to Move Beyond Raw Material Exports, Boost Value Addition
original_payload.original_body:
Ethiopia’s Deputy Prime Minister Temesgen Tiruneh has urged African countries to move beyond exporting raw materials and accelerate value addition, industrialization and intra-African trade to translate the continent’s economic potential into jobs, prosperity and improved living standards.
Speaking at a continental trade forum in Addis Ababa, Temesgen stressed that Africa must retain a greater share of the economic value generated from its natural resources, expanding production capacity and growing consumer markets.
“We are more than 1.5 billion people, young and ambitious. We have land, minerals, and growing markets. We have everything, except the habit of keeping the value we create,” he said.
“A free trade area on paper is not the goal. The goal is more trade among Africans, strong factories, more jobs, and better lives,” the Deputy PM underscored.
The forum, co-hosted by Ethiopia’s Ministry of Trade and Regional Integration and TradeMark Africa under the theme “Building Africa’s Exports Through Quality,” brings together policymakers, regulators, business leaders, researchers and development partners to explore ways of strengthening the continent’s export capacity and competitiveness.
The Deputy Prime Minister emphasized that realizing the full potential of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) requires more than removing trade barriers, calling for stronger industrial production, improved product quality and the development of competitive African manufacturing industries.
Against the backdrop of rising global protectionism and shifting supply chains, Temesgen called on African countries to strengthen their collective voice in international trade negotiations while investing in domestic quality infrastructure.
He underscored that product quality is fundamental to building trust and securing access to international markets.
“Quality is not just a technical matter. Quality is trust, and trust is the currency of trade,” he said, warning that the rejection of African products at international borders results in financial losses for exporters and undermines the continent’s commercial reputation.
He called for an integrated continental quality infrastructure that would allow products tested and certified in one African country to be recognized across other markets, reducing unnecessary compliance costs, delays and technical barriers to trade.
“No African producer should lose a sale because there is no laboratory to test the product or no certificate the buyer will accept,” he stressed.
Highlighting Ethiopia’s institutional reforms, Temesgen said the country had brought its standards, inspection, certification, metrology and accreditation institutions under a unified framework to help domestic businesses meet international market requirements.
“We want Made in Ethiopia to mean something everywhere it travels,” he added.
The Deputy Prime Minister further urged African governments and development partners to treat quality infrastructure as a strategic investment and expand support for small and medium-sized enterprises, particularly businesses led by women and young people.
He also emphasized the importance of modernizing transport corridors, logistics networks, cold-chain facilities and border systems to ensure that African products reach markets safely, efficiently and in good condition.
“A product that spoils on the way to market has not been exported; it has been wasted,” he cautioned.
Reaffirming Ethiopia’s commitment to advancing the forum’s outcomes and strengthening intra-African trade, Temesgen called for greater confidence in African products, production capacity and industrial potential.
“Let Made in Africa mean excellence. Let it mean reliability. Let it mean a promise kept,” he said.

items.title: African Leaders Call for Action, Domestic Investment to Advance Health Sovereignty

original_payload.original_title: African Leaders Call for Action, Domestic Investment to Advance Health Sovereignty
original_payload.original_body:
African leaders have called for stronger political commitment, increased domestic investment and concrete action to accelerate the continent’s transition toward health sovereignty, self-reliance and resilient healthcare systems.
Speaking at the Fifth International Conference on Public Health in Africa (CPHIA 2026) in Addis Ababa, African Union Commission Chairperson Mahmoud Ali Youssouf affirmed that public health security is the foundation of true sovereignty, underscoring its importance to Africa’s ability to safeguard its people and determine its own health future.
Tanzanian President Samia Suluhu Hassan, for her part, called for renewed collective action to translate commitments into tangible progress, strengthen national ownership and advance Africa’s health sovereignty.
Similarly, Sierra Leonean President Julius Maada Bio urged CPHIA 2026 to deliver more than declarations, calling for practical action, stronger partnerships and renewed commitment to saving lives across the continent.
Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye, for his part, called for a decisive shift from political commitments to increased domestic health financing, emphasizing that Africa’s health sovereignty begins with African investment.
The leaders’ calls come as the highly anticipated CPHIA 2026 officially opened in Addis Ababa early today, bringing together African heads of state, health ministers, policymakers, leading scientists and international partners to advance a new continental agenda for health security, self-reliance and sovereignty.
Co-hosted by the Government of Ethiopia and the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC), the five-day landmark gathering is taking place at the Addis International Convention Center from November 23 to 27.
Held under the theme “Africa’s Health Security and Sovereignty: Transformation from Health Dependency and Vulnerability to Ownership and Resilience,” the conference seeks to accelerate Africa’s transition from dependence on external health systems and assistance toward greater ownership of its health priorities, resources, technologies and institutions.
The messages from the four leaders highlight a common continental priority: translating political commitments into measurable progress through domestic financing, stronger partnerships, national ownership and coordinated action.
As the conference brings together African leadership and global health stakeholders, the discussions place the continent’s ambition to shape, finance and sustain its own health future firmly at the center of the global public health agenda.

items.title: Africa Must Leverage Product Quality for Competitive Advantage, Says Ethiopia’s Trade & Regional Integration Minister

original_payload.original_title: Africa Must Leverage Product Quality for Competitive Advantage, Says Ethiopia’s Trade & Regional Integration Minister
original_payload.original_body:
ddis Ababa, November 23, 2026 (ENA)— African nations must prioritize product quality to gain a competitive edge in global markets, Ethiopian Minister of Trade and Regional Integration, Yasmin Wohabrebbi, said on Monday.
Speaking at the opening of the Africa Trade Development Forum 2026 in Addis Ababa, Yasmin urged countries across the continent to move beyond exporting raw commodities and focus instead on producing globally competitive, value-added goods. She emphasized that adhering to high-quality standards is essential to expanding access to both regional and international markets.
"Africa’s trade prospects should not be measured by export volumes alone," Yasmin said.
The Minister further underscored the strategic role of quality in driving competitiveness and building consumer confidence.
Jointly organized by Ethiopia and TradeMark Africa under the theme “Building Africa’s Exports Through Quality,” the two-day forum convenes trade ministers, African Union officials, business leaders, regulators, standards institutions, and development partners.
Participants are exploring strategies to bolster Africa’s export capacity by harmonizing standards, strengthening quality infrastructure, upgrading certification systems, and promoting mutual recognition arrangements to facilitate smoother cross-border trade.
“Quality is no longer simply a technical requirement for accessing international markets,” she said. “It is a strategic instrument for competitiveness, consumer confidence, investment attraction, and sustainable economic growth.”
She identified trust as a cornerstone of Africa’s export ambitions, noting that buyers, regulators, and consumers must have confidence in the safety and standards of products originating from the continent.
“Ultimately, quality is about trust: the confidence of buyers, regulators, and consumers that an African product is safe and meets the standard it claims to meet,” she said, adding, “As tariffs fall under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), it is increasingly this trust that decides who gains access to the markets.”
The minister observed that despite Africa’s abundant natural resources, dynamic entrepreneurial potential, and expanding markets, the continent’s participation in global trade remains limited and heavily concentrated in primary commodities and raw minerals.
She stressed the need to strengthen local production, promote value addition, and develop competitive industries capable of meeting international quality requirements.
Highlighting Ethiopia’s efforts, she said the country has undertaken extensive economic and institutional reforms aimed at expanding productive capacity and improving the competitiveness of its export sectors.
The forum will also explore regional value chains, investment opportunities, and science, technology, and innovation, alongside the institutional systems required to enhance the credibility and market acceptance of African products.
Featuring panel discussions, exhibitions, and business-to-business engagements, the event is designed to strengthen partnerships and create new opportunities for trade and investment.
Organizers said the forum seeks to establish quality as a strategic foundation for Africa’s trade development, enabling businesses to expand intra-African commerce and compete more effectively in global markets.

items.title: Nigeria's president says he is also hit by water and power cuts plaguing country

original_payload.original_title: Nigeria's president says he is also hit by water and power cuts plaguing country
original_payload.original_body:
Nigeria's president says he is also hit by water and power cuts plaguing country
Image source,  Getty Images
Image caption,    Bola Tinubu promised to address the country's electricity problems while campaigning for the 2023 election
By  Mansur Abubakar    Reporting from Abuja
Published
23 November 2026, 11:15 GMT
Updated 4 hours ago
Nigeria's President Bola Tinubu says the presidential villa suffers from cuts in electricity and water - issues that are all too common for the country's ordinary citizens.
He said he was shaving last week when the water supply cut at the villa, known as Aso Rock, in Abuja.
He is seeking re-election next January and vowed to address these issues.
Tinubu made the disclosure on Sunday at a special prayer session organised in his honour by members of his family in Lagos.
He explained: "On the Wednesday of last week, I was shaving, and the water went off. In the villa, you won't know punishment dey dia too [there’s punishment there too in Nigerian pidgin].
"The water went off. So we will correct all this. No light, no water, no electricity, no development. We have just started. We can do it, and we will do it for Nigeria,” he said.
Aso Villa serves as both the office and official residence of the Nigerian president. It is situated at the base of Aso Rock in Abuja.
Last year, 10bn naira (£5.5m; $7.2m), was allocated in the budget for the installation of a solar mini-grid in the Aso Villa as part of efforts to address rising electricity bills and unstable power supply.
Some reports say it has been completed and is in the testing phase, with plans to fully disconnect the facility from the national grid soon.
Can Nigeria's president regain voters' trust after painful first term?
Published
12 November
Search and rescue teams race against time after Nigeria boat tragedy
Published
6 hours ago
Nigeria has long endured electricity shortages, but recent severe disruptions have been caused primarily by insufficient gas supplies and declining hydropower output, rather than the usual nationwide grid collapse.
Persistent blackouts in Lagos, Abuja and elsewhere have forced distribution companies to implement rotating power cuts, severely impacting households and businesses.
The country also suffers from chronic water shortages, the result of a structural crisis rooted in the gap between rapid urban population growth and decaying, inadequate public water infrastructure, leaving millions without reliable supplies, especially in Lagos.
Image source,  Getty Images
Image caption,    Many Nigerians rely on generators like these to power their homes and businesses
Tinubu made a high-profile electricity promise during the 2023 election campaign, but the exact wording and how binding it is has become a major point of contention ahead of the election on 16 January 2027.
In 2022, months before the last presidential election, Tinubu said: "Whichever way, by all means necessary, you will have electricity, and you will not pay for estimated bills any more. A promise made will be a promise kept.
"If I don't keep the promise and I come for a second term, don't vote for me, unless I give you adequate reasons why I couldn't deliver,” he said.
Despite the continuing power cuts, some of his supporters point to improved electricity supplies in rural areas as well as a recently approved $2bn (£1.5bn) investment in a new East–West Super Grid, designed to expand electricity transmission capacity and strengthen the national grid, as evidence that he is doing his best to keep to his promise.
Tinubu defeated the country’s former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar as well as former Anambra state governor Peter Obi in 2023 and the three are seen as the strongest contenders once again.

items.title: Prominent Zimbabwean preacher arrested on sexual assault allegations

original_payload.original_title: Prominent Zimbabwean preacher arrested on sexual assault allegations
original_payload.original_body:
Prominent Zimbabwean preacher arrested on sexual assault allegations
Image source,  H-Metro
Image caption,    Uebert Angel is still in police custody following a dramatic arrest over the weekend
By  Khanyisile Ngcobo    Reporting from Johannesburg
Published
3 hours ago
A well-known Zimbabwean preacher has been arrested on indecent assault and sodomy allegations, local police said.
Uebert Angel, who leads an international charismatic church with branches around the world, was arrested during a church service in Harare on Sunday. Pictures and footage of the dramatic arrest have since been circulated online.
In one video, a convoy of vehicles is seen escorting the self-styled prophet as he sits in the back of a police van surrounded by armed police officers.
The controversial founder of Spirit Embassy was also appointed Zimbabwe's special presidential envoy and ambassador-at-large to Europe and the Americas back in 2021 by President Emmerson Mnangagwa.
In 2023, he made headlines when an undercover report by Al Jazeera claimed that he had offered to use his diplomatic status to launder large amounts of money through a gold-smuggling scheme in the country.
According to the Qatar-based network, Angel, 48, told reporters working undercover that the scheme was approved by President Emmerson Mnangagwa.
Zimbabwean police only released a brief statement confirming his arrest but a member of his team told reporters the British Zimbabwean national was still in police custody and it was unclear when he'd make an appearance in court.
"It can be in the afternoon or tomorrow [Tuesday]. We are still within the legal framework [for him to appear in court]," Professor Lovemore Madhuku told state-owned broadcaster ZBC in a clip posted online.
This is not the first time the prominent preacher has been accused of improper behaviour.
A report by local online publication ZimLIVE in 2021 said that Angel had previously faced allegations of sexual impropriety from several women, at least five of whom are in England. The charismatic preacher has denied the allegations, the outlet added at the time.
Angel's church has branches in Zimbabwe, South Africa and the UK and he known for his ties to other African preachers like Malawian televangelist Shepherd Bushiri.

items.title: Kenya and DR Congo agree to restore ties after tensions over conflict

original_payload.original_title: Kenya and DR Congo agree to restore ties after tensions over conflict
original_payload.original_body:
Kenya and DR Congo agree to restore ties after tensions over conflict
Image source,  William Ruto/X
Image caption,    The meeting between Kenya's President William Ruto (left) and DR Congo's Félix Tshisekedi (centre) was hosted by Denis Sassou Nguesso (right)
By  Basillioh Rukanga
Published
23 November 2026, 08:53 GMT
Kenya's President William Ruto and his Congolese counterpart Felix Tshisekedi have agreed to restore full diplomatic ties between the two countries following tensions over the conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
Relations between the two countries have soured since 2023 when DR Congo accused Kenya of hosting leaders launching a rebel alliance, including the M23.
This led DR Congo to recall its envoy to Nairobi. Relations deteriorated further when Kinshasa refusing to accredit Kenya's nominated ambassador.
On Sunday, the two leaders affirmed their commitment to "sovereignty, territorial integrity, non-interference in the internal affairs of states".
The agreement was announced in a joint statement issued after the summit held in the town of Oyo in Congo-Brazzaville, facilitated by the nation's President Denis Sassou Nguesso, with Togolese leader Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé as mediator.
Tshisekedi and Ruto also agreed to "good neighbourliness and peaceful settlement of disputes" as well as "strengthen cooperation within regional mechanisms".
DR Congo and Kenya are both members of the East African Community (EAC).
DR Congo, which joined in 2022, is the latest entrant to the bloc, but its membership has been complicated by its accusation that Rwanda, a fellow member, backs the M23 rebels. Rwanda denies the claims despite overwhelming evidence.
DR Congo has also accused Kenya of hosting Congolese political and rebel leaders whom it says are working to destabilise the country.
When the Congo River Alliance (AFC), a political-military alliance including the M23, was launched in Nairobi in 2023, DR Congo responded by recalling its ambassador to Kenya.
The tensions were stoked further in March last year after Kenya named a consul-general to Goma, the capital of DR Congo's North Kivu region, after it fell to M23 forces, who control many eastern parts of the country.
DR Congo said naming the envoy amounted to disrespect for the country's territorial integrity and seemed to legitimise the group's occupation.
Suited and booted: How Joseph Kabila went from president to rebel leader
Published
31 October
Relations deteriorated further after Kenya hosted a meeting of Congolese opposition figures,  including former President Joseph Kabila , in October 2025.
Kabila was in 2025 sentenced to death in absentia on charges including war crimes and treason. He denied the accusations, but did not appear in court to defend himself.
He has since been named the leader of the Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN), the new rebel coalition that took over from the AFC.
Sunday's meeting between Ruto and Tshisekedi also included other issues including deepening trade cooperation, economic development, and regional integration.
The two also sought to collaborate to control the spread of the Ebola virus.
On Sunday, the head of the World Health Organization (WHO), Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, said the frequency of attacks across the country's east had increased since the end of October, seriously affecting the Ebola response.
Tedros said heavy fighting in an area close to where the Ebola outbreak first emerged had disrupted work and the wider Ebola response.
More than 5,700 people have died and 11,000 infected with Ebola in DR Congo since the outbreak was declared in May.
The latest outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo species of the virus, has spread beyond DR Congo borders, with cases reported in Kenya, Uganda and Nigeria.

items.title: Search and rescue teams race against time to find survivors after Nigeria boat tragedy

original_payload.original_title: Search and rescue teams race against time to find survivors after Nigeria boat tragedy
original_payload.original_body:
Search and rescue teams race against time to find survivors after Nigeria boat tragedy
Image source,  Bloomberg via Getty Images
Image caption,    Many Nigerian rely on boats to travel beyond their villages (file photo)
By   Makuochi Okafor   ,  BBC Africa   ,   Reporting from Lagos      and    Ondiro Oganga
Published
23 November 2026, 11:38 GMT
Updated 6 hours ago
Nigerian search and rescue teams are racing against time to find survivors after a boat carrying mourners travelling to a funeral capsized on Friday.
Twenty-nine bodies have been recovered and 50 people rescued so far, a spokesperson for the National Emergency Management Agency (Nema) told the BBC.
The government has responded by ordering stricter enforcement of safety standards on the country's inland waterways.
Overcrowding, poor maintenance and failure to observe safety regulations have contributed to previous deadly accidents on Nigeria's rivers.
The boat was travelling from Ayama community when it developed mechanical problems, according to police spokesperson Musa Mohammed.
Passengers asked the boat operator to steer towards land, but he allegedly declined, leading to the accident.
Survivors have described the panic that followed as passengers struggled to swim and stay afloat while waiting for emergency rescue services.
"As I swam, people were dragging me to the bottom, and I bit one woman and saved myself," Charity Ebikaboaere told local media outlet Arise News.
"Our things, our money, phones, everything lost, but me and my siblings are alive," said another survivor, Tari Samuel.
Why do Nigeria's boat disaster keep happening?
Published
20 July
Nema spokesman Manzo Ezekiel raised concerns about the use of untrained boat operators and passengers travelling without life jackets.
"Some of them believe they're from river areas and they know how to swim," he said, warning that familiarity with waterways should not replace basic safety precautions.
There have been reports that the boat was carrying more than 300 people but the Nema spokesperson said this wasn't correct. He did not say how many people were on board but said it was overcrowded.
The accident happened in a region where waterways are a key means of transport, especially for communities with limited road access.
"Overloading, speeding, recklessness and traveling without life jackets must stop. No journey is worth a life," Bayelsa Commissioner for Information Ebiuwou Koku-Obiyai said in a statement on Saturday.
Nigeria's President Bola Tinubu has relayed his condolences to the victims' families.
In a statement posted on X, Tinubu said he had directed relevant federal disaster response agencies to work together to ensure a successful rescue and recovery operation.
He also ordered that his election rally on Saturday, in Ibadan, Oyo State, be held without much fanfare in honour of those who lost their lives.
Boat accidents are a recurring problem in Nigeria, particularly in riverine communities where boats are a major means of transport.
In August, at least 50 people, mostly children, died after an overloaded boat capsized in the north-western Sokoto state. In January, at least 25 people died when a leaking boat capsized in Yobe state, in the north-east.

items.title: Ivory Coast star Pepe did not injure eyes staring at sun, say Villarreal

original_payload.original_title: Ivory Coast star Pepe did not injure eyes staring at sun, say Villarreal
original_payload.original_body:
Pepe did not injure eyes staring at sun, say Villarreal
Image source,  Getty Images
Image caption,    Nicolas Pepe (right) wore an eye mask on his return to the side following his eye operation in October
By  Tom Mallows   BBC Sport senior journalist
Published
22 November 2026
Villarreal say reports striker Nicolas Pepe needed eye surgery because he stared directly at the solar eclipse are "completely false".
In a statement, the Spanish club said an operation in October that ruled the 31-year-old out for six matches was "scheduled in advance" and "entirely unrelated" to the eclipse, which took place on 12 August.
Reports on social media suggested the former Arsenal forward had injured his eyes staring directly at the sun during the lunar event, with a video then emerging - purportedly from one of Pepe's social media accounts - showing him watching it in Spain.
"Villarreal CF, in response to reports published in various media outlets recently, clarifies that it is completely false that Nicolas Pepe's eye surgery has any connection to viewing the solar eclipse," said the club.
"The surgery had been scheduled in advance for reasons entirely unrelated to this event.
"The club urges accuracy and responsibility when reporting on matters related to its players' health."
Staring at an eclipse without protection can damage the retina, which sits at the back of the eye, and particularly those cells responsible for sharp central vision.
In the build-up to this summer's event,  experts warned  only genuine specially-designed solar eclipse glasses should be used, and that ordinary sunglasses or other devices were not enough to prevent potential damage.
Ivory Coast international Pepe has scored 14 goals in 86 appearances in all competitions for Villarreal after joining from Trabzonspor in 2024.
He cost Arsenal a then-club record £72m when he joined from Lille in the summer of 2019.
Pepe scored 27 goals in 112 games for the Gunners and had a loan spell at Nice before joining Trabzonspor on a free transfer.

items.title: South Sudan: MSF Suspends All Activities in Yei River County Following Abduction

original_payload.original_title: South Sudan: MSF Suspends All Activities in Yei River County Following Abduction
original_payload.original_body:
Juba — Médecins Sans Frontières/Doctors Without Borders (MSF) suspended all its activities for a minimum of three months starting Tuesday 17 November, in South Sudan’s Yei River County, Central Equatoria State, after armed assailants abducted an MSF staff member and a Ministry of Health midwife on Thursday 12 November. Although both staff members were released unharmed on Saturday 14 November, this incident highlights the continuation of violence against healthcare workers in South Sudan.
MSF denounces in the strongest terms the abduction of humanitarian and medical workers as utterly unacceptable. MSF calls upon authorities and other actors to take responsibility and act decisively to put an end to these incidents.
"The suspension of services was a painful and uneasy decision, given the people's needs in the area, particularly among vulnerable groups, such as pregnant and lactating women, children and the elderly," says Dr Ferdinand Atte, MSF's Head of Mission in South Sudan. "In addition, we had to suspend MSF’s support to the Ebola preparedness, in particular for the management of the isolation facility, which could have dramatic consequences in case of the outbreak in the area."

original_payload.original_body:
As government forces also expand their aerial arsenal, the strategic value of these systems complicates prospects for de-escalation.
The eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is rapidly emerging as a key theatre of drone warfare. State militaries and non-state actors alike are exploiting technological advances, a thriving military drone market and cheaper access to commercial aerial vehicles that can be adapted for conflict.
Since 2022 both the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (FARDC) and rebel groups like M23 have been ramping up drone acquisition and use. The Rwanda-backed rebels captured Goma in North Kivu in January 2025 and Bukavu in South Kivu a month later. Many experts  believe  these gains would have been impossible without an extensive arsenal of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs).

original_payload.original_body:
COP31 Ends Without Global Climate Agreement
The COP31 in Türkiye  closed  without an overarching climate deal after almost 200 countries could not agree on a consensus after two days of extended talks. The European Union, UK, Panama and others rejected the proposed Antalya Pact, which was marred by deep divisions on fossil fuels, climate finance and the 1.5C warming threshold. UN Secretary-General António Guterres expressed disappointment, and climate advocates denounced the failure to secure a clear commitment to move away from fossil fuels and to boost adaptation funding for vulnerable countries. The result leaves major questions unresolved on climate finance, energy transitions and support for communities facing worsening climate impacts for Africa and other developing countries. The target was scrapped in the final draft, which would have seen adaptation funding for developing countries ramped up to at least $120 billion a year by 2035. Despite the setback, separate initiatives on electrification and ocean protection offered some progress, with more than 90 countries supporting an electrification initiative.

items.title: Africa: The French-African Foundation Opens Applications For 2027 Young Leaders Cohort

original_payload.original_title: Africa: The French-African Foundation Opens Applications For 2027 Young Leaders Cohort
original_payload.original_body:
The French-African Foundation has officially opened applications on 17 November (until 16 December) for the 2027 intake of its flagship Young Leaders programme, with 30 standout individuals from across Africa and France set to join the influential cross-continental network.
Widely regarded as one of the most competitive leadership initiatives bridging Africa and France, the programme targets a new generation of decision-makers aged 28 to 40 – from entrepreneurs and corporate executives to diplomats, researchers, artists and civil society leaders.
Following in the footsteps of previous intakes - held under the joint patronage of the French President alongside African heads of state including Paul Kagame (Rwanda), Macky Sall (Senegal) and Nana Akufo-Addo (Ghana) - the 2027 cohort will once again benefit from backing at the highest political level.
Two immersive weeks across Africa and Paris
Over the course of a year, the 30 selected fellows gain direct access to heads of state, government ministers, investors and chief executives from major international and pan-African companies. The programme is anchored by two intensive, week-long residencies - one on the African continent and the other in Paris - designed to forge strategic alliances and spark peer-to-peer collaboration.
“We are looking for 30 exceptional individuals capable of transforming their sectors and building new alliances between Africa and France,” says Nachouat Meghouar, Managing Director of the French-African Foundation. “Our ambition is to open up the networks, opportunities and partnerships that will help take their ventures to the next level.”

items.title: Initiative « Une Semaine, Une Ecole » : Le DREN de Tahoua visite le CSP La Victoire

original_payload.original_title: Initiative « Une Semaine, Une Ecole » : Le DREN de Tahoua visite le CSP La Victoire
original_payload.original_body:
Tahoua, 23 Nov (ANP) – Le Directeur Régional de l’Education Nationale, de l’Alphabétisation et de la Promotion des Langues de Tahoua, M. Alhassane Ibounou, accompagné d’une forte délégation, était tôt ce matin du lundi 23 novembre 2026 dans les locaux du Complexe Scolaire Privé (CSP) La Victoire, relevant de l’inspection communale de l’enseignement primaire Tahoua 1.
Cette septième sortie hebdomadaire du responsable régional de l’éducation nationale s’inscrit dans le cadre de l’initiative « une semaine, une école » de la Ministre de l’Education Nationale, de l’Alphabétisation et de la Promotion des Langues, Dr Elisabeth Shérif. Le DREN et la délégation qui l’accompagne ont été accueillis à leur arrivée par les encadreurs pédagogiques de l’ICEP Tahoua 1 et l’ensemble du corps enseignant de l’école et de l’administration. Au mât du drapeau, la délégation du DREN a suivi avec succès l’exécution des deux hymnes, l’Honneur de la patrie et la Confédérale de l’AES.
Après la montée des couleurs, le représentant du personnel enseignant, a très succinctement présenté le CSP La Victoire, établissements qui a fait un taux d’admission de 85,24% à la session passée des examens du CFEPD et à l’entrée en classe de 6ème.
L’établissement compte cette année 68 candidats dont 30 filles sur un effectif de 523 élèves dont 239 filles. Cet effectif est pris en charge par 16 enseignants.
Prenant la parole pour la circonstance, le Directeur Régional de l’Education Nationale de Tahoua a de prime abord félicité le corps enseignant pour le taux exceptionnel en examen enregistré l’an passé et l’a exhorté à continuer dans ce sens pour aboutir cette année à un taux de 100% à la session 2027.
Le DREN a par la suite transmis les salutations et encouragements de la Ministre de l’Education Nationale, de l’Alphabétisation et de la Promotion des Langues pour l’effort et l’apport que l’enseignement privé apporte au système éducatif nigérien.
Après l’entretien direct avec les enseignants, le DREN de Tahoua a effectué quelques visites dans l’établissement. C’est ainsi qu’il a visité en premier lieu une classe de CM2 où il a prodigué des sages conseils aux candidats.
La deuxième visite a conduit la délégation du DREN au bureau du censeur du côté du secondaire pour vérifier les conditions de travail des agents.
Enfin, le DREN a visité une classe de terminale où il a également prodigué des sages conseils aux candidats. Cette dernière visite a mis fin à cette sortie du DREN de Tahoua au CSP LA Victoire.
